Title: Ringgit opens mostly higher as GDP growth beats forecasts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened mostly higher against a basket of major currencies on Monday after Malaysia's advance estimate of third-quarter 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth came in stronger than expected at 5.3 per cent.
Against the US dollar, the ringgit was little changed, quoted at 4.0790/0855 at 8 am compared with Friday's close of 4.0795/0835.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said stronger-than-expected economic growth could reinforce expectations of a potential normalisation of monetary policy.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia, in its advance GDP estimates released on Friday, reported that the economy grew by 5.3 per cent in the third quarter, following 6.0 per cent growth in the preceding quarter.
Meanwhile, concerns over the valuations of artificial intelligence-related stocks could prompt traders and investors to seek safe-haven assets, including US Treasury bonds, potentially lending support to the US dollar.
"Therefore, the ringgit-US dollar could trade in the range between RM4.07 and RM4.08 today," he told Bernama.
At the opening, the ringgit strengthened against the euro to 4.5791/5864 from 4.5911/5956 at Friday's close and edged up against the British pound to 5.4393/4480 from 5.4396/4449. However, it weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5849/5892 from 2.5831/5895.
Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit also traded mostly higher.
It edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 226.2/226.7 from 226.3/226.6 and the Philippine peso to 6.47/6.49 from 6.48/6.49.
The local currency also strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1882/1935 from 3.1889/1922 at Friday's close and the Thai baht to 12.2013/2320 from 12.2101/2268.

Title: RM1bil impairment unlikely to affect Public Bank's capital-return plan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd's RM1 billion goodwill impairment at its Hong Kong operations is unlikely to have a material direct impact on its RM3.5 billion capital-return plan, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The bank recently announced a full goodwill impairment of HK$1.96 billion (RM1 billion) at its 73.23 per cent-owned Hong Kong subsidiary, Public Financial Holdings Ltd, following an impairment assessment.
Public Bank said the non-cash charge could reduce its financial year 2026 (FY26) consolidated earnings per share and net assets per share by four sen each.
CIMB Securities estimated the impairment charge, after accounting for minority interests, at RM748.1 million, equivalent to 10 per cent of its previous FY26 reported net profit forecast.
The research firm, however, excluded the charge from its core net profit forecast.
It expects limited impact on Public Bank's regulatory capital, dividend capacity and underlying operations, as goodwill is already deducted when calculating Common Equity Tier 1 capital.
Bloomberg reported on Oct 16 that Japan's MS&AD Insurance Group was exploring an acquisition of LPI Capital Bhd, in which Public Bank acquired a controlling interest in December 2024.
CIMB Securities said a potential sale could unlock value for Public Bank, although it remained uncertain whether the bank would be willing to divest its stake, given the recent acquisition and the strategic importance of insurance to its banking business.
On the earnings front, the research firm expects Public Bank to post a largely flat core net profit of RM1.85 billion in the third quarter of FY26, up 0.5 per cent year-on-year and 1.5 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
This would bring its nine-month core net profit to RM5.43 billion, up 1.5 per cent year-on-year.
Earnings are expected to be supported by non-interest income from wealth management activities, including unit trusts and bancassurance, as well as foreign exchange activities.
However, these gains could be partly offset by subdued growth in fund-based income, with net interest margin expected to narrow by another three basis points quarter-on-quarter to 2.05 per cent.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Buy" rating on Public Bank but lowered its target price to RM5.35 from RM5.50, following downward revisions to its earnings forecasts and a weaker net interest margin outlook.
The firm cut its FY26, FY27 and FY28 net profit forecasts by 12.5 per cent, 2.1 per cent and 2.5 per cent, respectively.
The revisions reflect the one-off goodwill impairment at Public Financial and expectations of weaker margins.
Despite near-term margin pressure, CIMB Securities said Public Bank remained one of the banking sector's more attractive defensive investment options, backed by its core earnings, strong asset quality and RM3.5 billion capital-return plan.

Title: Mount Kinabalu records 239 emergency cases involving hikers since 2022
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A total of 239 emergency cases involving hikers who were injured or unable to continue their climb were recorded on Mount Kinabalu from 2022 until this month.
Sabah Fire and Rescue Department director Mohd Pisar Aziz said the figure highlights the need for continuous readiness among rescue teams at the state's iconic mountain, which attracts both domestic and international climbers.
He said that despite its beauty and appeal, Mount Kinabalu poses high safety risks, with every incident demanding thorough assessment, appropriate action, and effective coordination among all parties involved.
"Mountain rescue operations are not easy due to steep routes, rocky and slippery surfaces, rapidly changing weather conditions, and communication constraints.
"These factors often pose major challenges to rescue teams, particularly when dealing with victims who are injured and unable to move on their own.
"Therefore, the department remains committed to providing emergency assistance and conducting search and rescue operations within the department's jurisdiction, competency, and capabilities," he said.
He said this at a dinner celebrating the success of 26 participants in the Jelajah Akinabalu 4095: Sinergi Dua Entiti programme organised by the Media Prima Club (MPC) here last night.
Also present were Sabah Fire and Rescue Department deputy director Ashari Johari, Agrobank Group Marketing and Communication head Intan Syazwani Isa, and Agrobank Sabah Sales and Services Department head Samuel Michael.
All 26 participants from MPC and Kelab Agrobank successfully scaled the 4,095.2-metre peak of Mount Kinabalu two days ago.
The programme, held in collaboration with Kelab Agrobank, was joined by representatives from the New Straits Times, Berita Harian, Harian Metro and TV3, alongside seven Kelab Agrobank members.
[[nid:1558632]]
Elaborating further, Pisar said operations on Mount Kinabalu require personnel who possess not only physical and mental endurance, but also technical skills and the ability to make decisions in high-risk field situations.
He said the capability and commitment of the rescue teams were demonstrated during Ops Mauro, an operation to bring down a Croatian climber that took five days, starting Sept 6.
He noted that the operation showcased the dedication and endurance required to execute rescue missions in mountainous terrain.
"Bringing the victim down safely required careful planning, coordination among personnel, and the use of methods and equipment suited to the terrain.
"In such operations, every decision carries significant weight. Route selection, casualty management, weather conditions, and personnel safety must be continuously prioritised throughout the operation.
"To enhance the efficiency of rescue missions along challenging trails, the department has leveraged technological innovations such as the Body Harness Carrier (BHC), which was specifically developed based on actual field requirements," he said.
He added that personnel safety and continuous risk assessment remain top priorities to ensure the success of every search and rescue (SAR) operation.
Meanwhile, he said the partnership forged through the climbing programme organised by MPC reflects the close ties between the department and media practitioners.
"The media is a strategic partner for the department in delivering information, raising public awareness on safety, and highlighting the roles and responsibilities of firefighters to the public.
"I hope this expedition served as a meaningful experience for all participants while offering an opportunity to observe firsthand the uniqueness of Mount Kinabalu and the challenges faced by mountain rescue teams," he said.
Pisar added that the relationship between the department and the media extends beyond news reporting to building public awareness and understanding of safety and emergency preparedness.
He said accurate writing, reporting, and information sharing enable the media to convey safety messages to a broader audience.
"Responsibly reported information helps the public understand the real challenges faced by rescue teams.
"I hope this expedition allowed the media to see the uniqueness and challenges of Mount Kinabalu firsthand, bringing home experiences that can be shared with the public.
"May the strategic relationship continue to be strengthened for the benefit of the community and mutual safety," he said.

Title: Haze: 27 areas record unhealthy API readings, Johan Setia highest at 173
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings were recorded in 27 areas nationwide as of 8am today, with Johan Setia in Selangor logging the highest level at 173.
Nilai in Negri Sembilan followed at 169, while Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded 168.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System, Johor had the highest number of areas in the unhealthy category at seven: Pasir Gudang (164), Tangkak (164), Batu Pahat (159), Kota Tinggi (158), Kluang (155), Larkin (153), and Pengerang (147).
All three monitoring stations in Melaka recorded unhealthy readings, with Alor Gajah at 165 and Bandaraya Melaka at 164.
In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded 165 and Port Dickson 153.
In Selangor, Petaling Jaya recorded 160, followed by Klang (158), Banting (156), and Shah Alam (155).
In the Federal Territories, Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 162, while Cheras and Putrajaya each registered 155.
In Pahang, Rompin recorded 158, and Indera Mahkota, Kuantan, 139.
In Sarawak, Kuching and the Serian district police headquarters each recorded 153, while Samarahan registered 138.
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded 108.
Meanwhile, Segamat in Johor recorded the highest moderate reading at 99, followed by Tawau in Sabah at 98.
Only three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah (50) and Kota Bharu (50) in Kelantan, and Limbang (47) in Sarawak.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.

Title: Trump endorses Netanyahu, warns Israel against choosing rival in tight election
Article:
JERUSALEM: US President Donald Trump endorsed on Sunday his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel's close-fought parliamentary election on Oct 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister's bid to win a new mandate.
Netanyahu touted his close relationship with the US president in a video released by his Likud party, saying that together they had "crushed Iran" and adding that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to "elminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner."
The endorsement comes less than two weeks before Israel's first vote since the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, which opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for after allegedly ignoring warnings.
Trump and Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight election race, have worked closely together on Israel's multi-front wars after the Hamas-led attack, including bombarding Iran, and the endorsement could be a boon to his re-election campaign.
"Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using a common nickname for the Israeli leader.
"This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much. Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel."
The election is seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, who quickly thanked the US leader for his support on Sunday.
"Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!" he wrote on X.
"I ask you to listen carefully to what President Trump said this evening," Netanyahu told voters. "He said that together we have accomplished extraordinary things... But there is still a mission to complete."
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned Netanyahu was "driving America into another war."
"Last time you wanted to 'finish the job', Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful; we have unfinished jobs too," Araghchi wrote on X.
Trump joined Netanyahu in a US-Israeli attack on Iran in late February but agreed to a ceasefire in April in the face of widespread US public opposition to the war, which had sent oil prices spiralling.
Speaking at an event in August, Netanyahu said Trump "is our greatest friend, one of the greatest friends we have had in the White House."
But relations between the two have at times been strained on Iran, with Netanyahu saying no diplomatic agreement was possible with Iran's leadership, while Trump sought a negotiated end to the months-long conflict.
- VOTER WARNING -
The endorsement comes after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing "crisis" in the occupied West Bank after an American photojournalist for The Washington Post was injured in a brutal attack by Israeli settlers.
"We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Rubio told reporters Saturday. Netanyahu's office said it was investigating the circumstances around the attack.
With Israel and Netanyahu looking increasingly isolated on the world stage, Trump's support is vital.
Netanyahu, who turns 77 on Oct 21, is Israel's longest-serving prime minister, having served on and off for more than 19 years.
The wily political operator returned to power in December 2022, bringing in once-shunned ultra-nationalists and quickly tried to rein in the judiciary, which is examining corruption charges that could land him in jail.
His main election rival is opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the centre-right Yashar party and a former military chief who regularly accuses Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for the Oct 7 attack.
About seven million Israelis will be eligible to vote in the legislative election.
Current polls show that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor that led by Eisenkot is in a position to win the 61 seats needed to control the 120-seat parliament and form a governing coalition.
Eisenkot said that only Israelis could choose who they want to run the country.
Speaking at a conference in Tel Aviv, Eisenkot said he "admires" Trump "but Israel is a democratic country, only Israelis can choose their leaders."
But Trump warned against Israel electing "anyone other than Bibi", writing that if voters chose one of his rivals, "America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil slips as Trump's sanction waiver may lead to more Russian fuel supplies
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices slipped on Monday after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports.
Brent crude futures fell US$1.43, or 1.3 per cent, to US$108.43 a barrel by 2340 GMT after settling at its highest since May 19 on Friday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$100.88 a barrel, down 53 cents, or 0.52 per cent.
Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving key sanctions and tariffs under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who want to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine.
However, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president will use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of the waiver.
The move comes after Trump struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to export diesel to the United States. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said these US actions will hurt Ukraine.
Brent crude oil briefly touched US$110 a barrel on Friday for the first time since May as tensions and security threats in the Middle East raised concerns over the safety of shipping and tighter global energy supplies.
Intensified attacks on commercial vessels cut Gulf crude flows sharply to about 8.5 million barrels per day on a seven-day average last week from more than 20 million bpd the week before, analytics firm Kpler said in a Friday note. At least 10 confirmed incidents involving commercial vessels were reported last week, it added.
Potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war, Egypt said it is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.

Title: Melaka polls: Pas machinery mobilised, PN confident of defeating PH
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is confident of defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) in next month's Melaka state election.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said support for the coalition had been positive so far.
"We are confident of challenging PH in Melaka with the support we have. Survey data also shows that Melaka voters continue to support PN and Pas, as they did in the last general election.
"Pas has also mobilised its machinery and is taking every contest seriously. What matters is that our machinery continues to engage with the people, not just ahead of state elections, unlike other parties," he said when contacted.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nomination day scheduled for Oct 31.
Melaka has 28 state seats. In the previous state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats, PH secured five and PN took two.

Title: M40 aid, Madani school funding among issues in Dewan Rakyat today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Financial aid for M40 households, funding allocations for the Madani school and Kampung Angkat programmes, and the effectiveness of the Tourism Compliance Focus Zone (ZTPP) initiative will be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament website, Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah) will ask the finance minister about measures to assist M40 households no longer eligible for targeted aid but affected by the rising cost of living.
Adnan will also inquire about potential mechanisms to reassess eligibility based on current income and expenditure.
Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman anak Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the finance minister to provide a detailed breakdown of the RM50 million and RM200 million spent on the Madani school and Kampung Angkat programmes, respectively, to ensure transparency regarding their financial impact and the actual number of beneficiaries under the People's Housing Programme (PPR).
Hassan Saad (PN-Baling) will ask the domestic trade and cost of living minister for performance indicators used to evaluate the ZTPP programme's effectiveness in curbing price-gouging complaints.
Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) is set to ask about the implementation status of the National Women's Policy 2025-2030.
Meanwhile, Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) will ask the communications minister whether the ministry plans to extend social media age limits to online gaming platforms with large numbers of child and teenage users.
Following Question Time, the House will resume debates at the policy stage on the Supply Bill 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, presented the 2027 Budget on Oct 9.
According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, policy-stage debates on Budget 2027 will run until Oct 22, followed by four days of ministerial winding-up sessions beginning Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting spans 37 days, concluding on Dec 8.

Title: Nikkei slides on US tech selloff, oil-driven rate fears
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average tumbled on Monday as a selloff in US technology stocks and rising oil prices fuelled concerns about inflation and higher interest rates.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 fell 2.05 per cent to 63,984.45 in early trading. The broader Topix slipped 1.22 per cent to 4,016.34.
The decline in Japanese equities followed a weak session on Wall Street on Friday, weighed down by losses in artificial intelligence- and chip-related stocks.
A more than three per cent jump in oil prices also added to inflationary concerns, which have been a key driver of market volatility amid expectations of further monetary tightening by central banks.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Monday that underlying inflation is "quite close" to the central bank's two per cent target, heightening the importance of anchoring inflation around that level.
"While chip-related stocks drag the index down, buying of value and defensive stocks should underpin the market," Yuta Okamoto, market analyst at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Laboratory, wrote in a note.
There were 78 advancers in the Nikkei 225 against 147 decliners, with no stocks unchanged.
The largest losers were Taiyo Yuden, down 7.42 per cent, followed by Sumitomo Electric Ind., 5.96 per cent lower, and Sumco, which lost 5.88 per cent.
The largest percentage gainers in the index were Toho , up 3.64 per cent, followed by Baycurrent, 2.80 per cent higher, and Aeon, which gained 2.14 per cent.

Title: Bomb threat forces Tel Aviv-Vienna flight to divert to Bulgaria
Article:
SOFIA: A bomb threat against an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna on Sunday forced the plane to divert to Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian authorities and the airline.
The Austrian Airlines crew decided to make an emergency landing in Sofia after reportedly receiving a bomb threat as they neared Romania, Bulgaria's transport ministry said in a statement, adding that the passengers were evacuated from the aircraft after landing.
The Bulgarian air force scrambled a MiG-29 fighter jet to escort the airliner as part of established procedures, the transport ministry said.
The airline told AFP that 51 passengers and six crew were aboard the flight, and that a security search of the aircraft – an Airbus A320 – was launched after it safely landed in Sofia about a half hour after the threat.
"Once the search of the aircraft is complete, the passengers will be rebooked onto alternative flights as quickly as possible," the airline said.
According to Flightradar24 data, the aircraft, registered OE-LZE, entered Romanian airspace at around 9.10pm before turning south and heading back towards Bulgaria, where it landed in Sofia.
Data from another flight-tracking platform, ADS-B Exchange, indicates that the aircraft was transmitting squawk code 7700 – a signal for a general emergency – at around the same time.
The transport ministry said that a crisis response team has been set up and the relevant authorities have launched an investigation into the incident.
In a separate incident late last month, the co-pilot aboard a flydubai airline flight headed to Tel Aviv from Dubai attacked the captain and allegedly planned to intentionally crash the plane but was stopped by the captain, passengers and crew.
Last week, Croatia and Germany both scrambled fighter jets after a commercial flight from the Greek holiday island of Corfu to the German city of Nuremberg accidentally sent out a hijacking alert.--AFP

Title: Lorry driver held after container crushes car, killing father and daughter
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A 49-year-old lorry driver has been detained after a container fell onto a car, killing a father and daughter near Sepanggar Port yesterday.
Mohd Jadi Pelbi, 53, and his daughter, Norfaieza Mohd Jadi, 24, were trapped inside their Toyota Avanza when the container crushed the car at Jalan Sepanggar at 6.15pm.
Kota Kinabalu police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said preliminary investigations found that the Hino container lorry had stopped by the roadside to load a container onto its trailer.
He said the lorry driver was loading the container when it suddenly became unstable and fell to the right, crushing the victims' car as it travelled along the right lane towards Sepanggar Port.
"Both victims were trapped inside the car and were extricated by firefighters at 9.55pm," he said when contacted today.
Medical personnel from Likas Hospital pronounced both victims dead at the scene at 9.58pm.
Their bodies were sent to Queen Elizabeth I Hospital's forensic department for post-mortem examinations.
Shahrudin said the lorry driver had been detained to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Those with information on the incident can contact investigating officer Inspector Brymenedren Godon at 010-7768802 or visit the nearest police station.
Firefighters used two cranes to move the container and free the car trapped beneath it. The operation took more than three hours.

Title: Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver, accuses Zelenskyy of prolonging war
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, while once again accusing Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war.
"My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
The remarks come after Trump signed an executive order late Friday waiving broad new sanctions mandated by legislation named for the late US senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Ukraine's defence.
Trump has also temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel, allowing large quantities to flow into global markets in a bid to lower fuel prices ahead of US elections early next month.
The diesel deal was met with shock by Kyiv and its allies and sparked a feud between Trump and Zelenskyy that has seen their roller-coaster relationship plummet again.
"Great progress is being made" in talks on the war, "and that includes current hostage negotiations!" Trump said.
"Signing that document at this time will do that, and I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" he said, though it was unclear to what document he was referring.
Asked for more clarity on the statement, the White House did not immediately respond to AFP.
"Perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way, and will, unless stupid people get in the way," Trump added.
He then reiterated his accusation that Ukraine was purposefully targeting Russian refineries to attempt to hurt the Republican Party in the Nov 3 election.
Polling shows Trump's party heading for a likely drubbing in the election, with many voters deeply upset by fuel costs, which have soared since the Iran war began in late February.
"Zelenskyy is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target, knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States," Trump said.
"Zelenskyy doesn't care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him, and that Crooked Joe Biden gave him in the past, he doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did," he added.--AFP

Title: Frail Indonesian markets reel after MSCI shock warning
Article:
SINGAPORE: Indonesian markets face a tense start on Monday after a warning from MSCI over possible expulsion from some of its indexes next year rattled already fragile investor sentiment and sparked a furious selloff in the world's worst-performing stock market.
Jakarta stocks sank 11.6 per cent on Friday, the benchmark's biggest one-day drop in nearly three decades, taking year-to-date losses to 40 per cent, after MSCI said it was considering shifting Indonesia to "standalone" status from its current "emerging markets" mantle.
The index provider had threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status in January because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour but said on Friday the lack of progress in remedying those concerns meant even a downgrade to that status would not reflect the severity of the issues.
A shift to standalone status would risk cutting Southeast Asia's biggest economy off from international capital, relegate it to an investment backwater and club it with a group of standalone markets that includes Lebanon and Zimbabwe.
The more-severe-than-expected move has sharpened the focus on efforts by Jakarta to allay the long-standing concerns. On Friday, an Indonesian regulator unveiled sanctions against those linked to alleged trading manipulation in shares of three firms.
"The burden of proof has shifted: avoiding reclassification will require clear evidence that the announced reforms have been consistently implemented and materially improved market functioning," strategists at Goldman Sachs said in a note.
Goldman Sachs estimates a full MSCI removal could trigger US$5.6 billion of passive outflows. Active funds benchmarked to these indexes hold more than US$8 billion, although any selling would be discretionary rather than benchmark-driven, they wrote.
Foreign investors have net sold US$4.88 billion worth of Indonesian stocks so far this year, on track for the biggest annual outflow in at least 16 years.
Aninda Mitra, head of Asia macro and investment strategy at BNY Investments, said foreign equity exposure to Indonesia has shrunk to the point where "there may not be much more downside from here."
"But at the same time, even if there are some interesting and fundamentally sound companies and banks, attracting sufficiently large amounts of capital will be tougher in this environment," he said.
MSCI's warning raises the stakes for the government of President Prabowo Subianto, which has faced a series of setbacks this year, with Moody's and Fitch having cut their sovereign rating outlooks to negative earlier in 2026.
Investors are also fretting over the ramifications beyond the US$500 billion stock market, with the rupiah weakening to 18,000 per dollar, not far from the record low of 18,190 hit in June.
"Our bigger concern is not index-related selling itself," said Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments in Singapore, "but the potential near-term spillover into the rupiah and domestic bond yields, where market dislocation could translate into tighter financial conditions and a more meaningful impact on the real economy."

Title: Indonesia Stock Exchange cuts its lower auto-rejection limit to 7pct from 15pct
Article:
JAKARTA: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Monday it cut its lower auto-rejection limit to seven per cent from 15 per cent, effective immediately and to be reassessed periodically.
"This adjustment is aimed at giving investors an opportunity to evaluate and digest available information, helping them make better investment decisions based on Indonesia's economic fundamentals," the exchange said in a statement.

Title: MBSB explores acquisitions to fuel next growth phase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MBSB Bhd is exploring further acquisitions, including mortgage portfolios, credit card businesses and takaful operations, as it seeks to expand its domestic presence and achieve greater economies of scale.
Chairman Datuk Wan Kamaruzaman Wan Ahmad said the group is considering acquiring financial institutions or selected assets from other industry players as part of its longer-term growth strategy.
"We are looking at all those possibilities and angles," he told Business Times in an interview.
Wan Kamaruzaman said MBSB is particularly interested in exploring mortgage portfolios, while a credit card business could be established organically or acquired from an existing operator.
Its wholly owned banking subsidiary, MBSB Bank Bhd, currently offers debit cards but is not listed as a credit card issuer by Bank Negara Malaysia, making the segment a potential new avenue for growth.
Takaful operations are another potential area of expansion, said Wan Kamaruzaman.
He said any potential acquisition would have to complement MBSB's existing operations and strategic requirements, with the group's Islamic banking focus limiting its options to Syariah-compliant businesses.
Nevertheless, he said opportunities existed among smaller, specialised financial services providers, including operators whose shareholders might be looking to exit their investments.
Asked whether MBSB would consider acquisitions overseas, Wan Kamaruzaman said the group would remain focused on Malaysia for now, with no immediate plans to expand abroad.
He said the group would consider international expansion only when it had achieved sufficient size and financial strength.
The potential acquisitions form part of MBSB's efforts to build greater scale in an increasingly competitive banking industry.
"Banking is about scale. And when you don't have scale, you need to know your niche," he said.
Wan Kamaruzaman said MBSB has the potential to grow its asset base to between RM100 billion and RM120 billion over the longer term.
He said a larger balance sheet would allow the group to benefit from economies of scale, improve operating efficiency and generate better returns.
MBSB's total assets stood at RM69.1 billion as at end-June 2026.
Still, Wan Kamaruzaman said the group would remain cautious in expanding its financing portfolio to avoid accumulating further impaired financing.
The group's gross impaired financing ratio improved slightly to 6.23 per cent as at end-June 2026, from 6.33 per cent at end-2025. However, it remained higher than the 5.33 per cent recorded at end-2024.
The ratio is also higher than the banking industry average of around two per cent.
MBSB has the backing of its major shareholders, the Employees Provident Fund and Permodalan Nasional Bhd, an important advantage in pursuing its longer-term ambitions.
The potential expansion comes as MBSB prepares a new four-year strategic plan covering 2027 to 2030, as its existing FLIGHT26 transformation programme comes to an end.
MBSB previously expanded through the acquisition of Asian Finance Bank in 2018, which established its Islamic banking platform, followed by the acquisition of Malaysian Industrial Development Finance Bhd in 2023.
The group is still working to improve integration and operating efficiency following those acquisitions.
Wan Kamaruzaman said MBSB's next phase of growth would require a combination of scale, prudent financing decisions and a clear focus on businesses where it could compete effectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Can Gamuda meet FY27 earnings projections?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has been in the news for securing billions of ringgit of contracts. In fact, in the financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY26) alone, the construction group has secured RM36 billion worth of new contracts.
That number has fueled market optimism for Gamuda's share price since March 31. Between then and October 16, Gamuda's share price increased by 28.7 per cent to close at RM4.78 per share.
However, some observers pointed out that the market is too optimistic on Gamuda's earnings prospects. While the group had secured triple the value of construction jobs in FY26 compared with in FY24, its margins have been declining.
It is also worth noting that about a year ago, the market had expected for Gamuda to record about RM1.8 billion of net profits in FY26. On Aug 19, 2025, the counter hit RM5.80 apiece, the highest since the stock was split on Dec 19, 2024.
The counter then went on a prolonged decline to RM3.70 on March 31, some 36.2 per cent lower, as it became clear that Gamuda could not meet the earnings forecast.
This raises the question whether Gamuda can meet the earnings forecast for the financial year ending July 31, 2027 (FY27) of RM1.4 billion, based on the consensus estimates of analysts covering the stock.
"Yes, Gamuda's margins have been declining, and moving forward if there were to be any margin lift, it's not going to be big. Say FY26 margin was five per cent, maybe FY27 only slightly higher at 5.2 per cent," says an analyst with a bank's research outlet.
Gamuda's net profit margins in FY26 was 5.98 per cent, which was the lowest over the last six financial years. In FY21, Gamuda's net profit margins was 17.97 per cent, when the group earned RM632.19 million out of RM3.52 billion revenue.
Except for in FY22 when Gamuda's net margins jumped to 24.21 per cent due to a one-off exceptional gain from the disposal of its highway assets, the rate has been declining year over year.
The declining margin coincides with Gamuda's expansions overseas. In FY21, overseas revenue was RM705.3 million, or 16.4 per cent of total, while net profit was RM97.6 million, making up 19.9 per cent of the total.
In FY26, total overseas revenue stood at RM11.07 billion, or 59.5 per cent of total. However, overseas net profits were only RM514.06 million, or 48.9 per cent of the total, despite contributing the larger portion to total revenue.
This shows that net profit margin of Gamuda's overseas ventures – both in construction and property development – was only 4.64 per cent in FY26. Gamuda's net profit margin for overseas ventures has been declining.
In FY22, Gamuda's overseas ventures returned 13.1 per cent. It then declined to 8.9 per cent in FY23, to 5.2 per cent in FY24 and FY25.
This shows that returns from Gamuda's large overseas ventures are getting thinner by the year.
Meanwhile, the group's orderbooks are heavy on overseas contracts. As of July 2026, Gamuda's unbilled orderbooks from overseas contracts stood at 57 per cent of the total, with Australian contracts making up 37 per cent of the total.
Since July 2026, Gamuda has secured a total RM8.2 billion worth of new contracts from Australia and RM2.7 billion from Taiwan.
In comparison, the group secured a RM1.7 billion hyperscale data centre job in Port Dickson and announced a joint venture with SD Guthrie Bhd and Gentari to develop a 680 MWac hybrid solar photovoltaic project with a battery energy storage system (BESS) in Perak.
These new contracts brought Gamuda's outstanding orderbook to RM62 billion.
"They argue that now the Malaysia orderbook is around 50 per cent vs Australia's which is around 30%. But the reality is the majority of new jobs will still come from Australia, and the margins are lowest among their operating geographical locations," says the analyst.
Beside overseas margins are usually lower than domestic, Gamuda's declining margin is also due to the profit recognition timing. At the moment, the existing contracts in Australia and Taiwan are at the early stage of execution.
An observer puts it that Gamuda is transitioning into heavier execution of the orderbook in FY27.
"As Gamuda's orderbook transitions into heavier execution, over 90 per cent of expected FY27 construction revenue is directly supported by existing contracts, driving projected construction revenue growth of 50 to 60 per cent this year, and a further around 20 per cent in FY28.
"Profitability will be further enhanced by a favourable project execution mix, high-margin property launches, and higher returns from its growing 6GW renewable energy portfolio," says the observer.
If Gamuda's construction revenue grew by 50 to 60 per cent in FY27, this means that it would reach between RM22.3 billion and RM23.8 billion, from RM14.9 billion in FY26. Assuming that net profit margins stays at five per cent, Gamuda could earn RM1.1 billion to RM1.2 billion.
That is not far off from the RM1.4 billion forecast net profit that the market is ascribing on the group. Another RM200 million to RM300 million of net profits could come from its property development segment.
Another risk factor is Gamuda's net gearing, which stood at more than the self-imposed 70 per cent ceiling as of end FY26. Total borrowings reached RM14.1 billion against RM4.7 billion of cash and marketable securities, leaving net debt of RM9.4 billion.
Short-term borrowings more than doubled to RM6.3 billion from a year ago, following land acquisitions in Vietnam and Singapore. Meanwhile, operating cash flow improved to RM808 million from a RM78 million outflow in FY25.
An observer said that Gamuda's rapid orderbook conversion, and bullet payments from the sold-out Eaton Park development in Vietnam, as well as expected cash inflows of RM5 billion over the next two years, will accelerate deleveraging from FY27 onwards.
The question now for Gamuda is execution, whether the group can actually grow its construction revenue by 50 to 60 per cent in FY27, or if the construction margins can start to recover.
In a note published on Sept 29, CGS International stated that Gamuda had raised its construction revenue projections for FY27 to FY28 which assumes a 30 per cent compound annualised growth rate (CAGR).
The 60 per cent year-on-year growth for FY27 assumes largely just its orderbook of RM61 billion, with minimal assumption of new wins. As of September, 91 per cent of the orderbook has yet to reach peak progress.
The orderbook is likely to stay at RM60 billion as of the end of the year, which is 20 per cent above target, said CGI International.
"This, together with better earnings delivery [with earnings per share (EPS) CAGR of 20 per cent between 2026 and 2028], could lead to a sustainable share price re-rating.
"We do not discount upside to FY27 forecast EPS given that three of its projects in New South Wales will be completed earlier than expected, where there is an incentive for early delivery," stated CGS International in the report.

Title: France's debt reckoning: The price of sovereignty
Article:
France's next political contest will also be a test of fiscal credibility. On 6 Oct, Marine Le Pen presented a programme promising €140 billion in spending cuts by 2032, net of at least €30 billion in tax cuts, according to Reuters. For a politician identified with national sovereignty, the message was revealing: political ambition now requires financial reassurance.
France has not defaulted. Its predicament is more gradual, but consequential. Successive governments have accumulated obligations that increasingly constrain their successors. The question is whether its political system can agree on an adjustment that investors will finance and citizens will accept.
The Cost of Political Delay
The European Commission's May 2026 assessment put France's public debt at 115.6 per cent of GDP in 2025 and its deficit at 5.1 per cent. It projected debt rising to 118.1 per cent in 2026 and 120.2 per cent in 2027. These projections are conditional, but their direction illustrates the challenge.
France's difficulties predate Le Pen's programme. Persistent deficits, weak growth and resistance to reforms have narrowed the government's choices. There is no painless combination of spending restraint, taxation and stronger growth. Delaying a settlement does not remove these choices; it can make them more expensive.
Borrowing costs require careful interpretation. French bond yields respond to eurozone interest-rate expectations and inflation, as well as domestic political risk. The gap between French and comparable German yields offers a clearer indication of relative market concern, although it is not a pure measure of fiscal credibility.
Nor do higher market yields immediately reprice the entire debt stock. Their effects accumulate as governments refinance maturing obligations and issue new debt. That gradual transmission gives policymakers time to respond. It also allows them to underestimate a burden that is still building.
France retains a diversified economy, substantial taxation capacity and deep financial markets. The danger is not that these strengths suddenly disappear. It is that interest payments absorb resources needed for investment, public services and protection against future shocks.
The fiscal task must therefore extend beyond cutting expenditure. Adjustment that damages productive investment or weakens growth can make the debt ratio harder to stabilise. Credibility depends on what is changed, how quickly, and whether the settlement can endure.
Le Pen's Credibility Test
Le Pen's announcement deserves scrutiny on precisely these terms. Its significance lies in the attempt to reconcile economic nationalism with fiscal restraint. A movement that promises to restore national control must also explain how it would finance the exercise of that control.
The announced savings remain political commitments. Their credibility depends on a transparent baseline, a realistic timetable and measures capable of surviving legal, administrative and parliamentary scrutiny.
Fraud prevention illustrates the difficulty. Recovering unpaid taxes is desirable, but anticipated recoveries cannot be treated as assured revenue. Administrative savings require decisions about staffing, services and responsibilities. Changes to France's financial relationship with the European Union involve obligations and negotiations, not simply unilateral announcements.
Tax reductions compound the challenge. A programme promising both lower taxation and substantial deficit reduction must explain which spending commitments will change and how essential services will be protected. Broad assurances about efficiency cannot settle those distributional questions.
The same standard should apply to every French party. Incumbents deserve no exemption because their language sounds reassuring; challengers deserve no presumption of competence because their promises are ambitious. Fiscal credibility must be demonstrated through coherent measures and plausible assumptions.
Giorgia Meloni's Italy offers a useful, limited comparison. Reuters' Breakingviews analysis argues that Le Pen faces a harder task in translating a nationalist platform into investor confidence, particularly given France's fragmented parliamentary landscape. The relevant lesson is the importance of governing capacity, rather than political branding.
Markets may welcome an announcement and subsequently reconsider it. Durable confidence requires evidence that a government can secure approval, implement its programme and sustain public consent. A favourable trading session cannot substitute for that work.
Sovereignty Has a Financing Cost
France's predicament exposes a tension within modern democracy. Voters authorise governments to make choices. Investors determine the terms on which they are prepared to finance borrowing. Neither source of influence eliminates the other.
Markets are not infallible arbiters of the public interest. They can exaggerate risks and react excessively to uncertainty. Nevertheless, a government that depends on continual borrowing cannot disregard the price investors demand.
Eurozone membership shapes France's options. Paris cannot independently set monetary policy or adjust a national exchange rate. It also benefits from a shared currency and common institutions. These arrangements provide support while limiting unilateral action; they do not remove the need for sustainable national budgets.
For Malaysia, the comparison is instructive without being exact. A national currency and monetary policy provide additional adjustment instruments. They do not guarantee greater fiscal space: inflation, exchange-rate pressures, debt composition and investor confidence still constrain policy. The lesson is to preserve flexibility through credible institutions and budgets, rather than assume that currency sovereignty makes borrowing constraints disappear.
France must also preserve the political legitimacy of adjustment. Citizens are more likely to accept difficult measures when burdens are distributed fairly, essential services remain credible and the government explains what its programme is intended to achieve.
Restoring confidence therefore requires more than persuading creditors that the accounts will improve. It requires persuading citizens that the adjustment will protect the country's capacity to prosper.
Political sovereignty supplies the authority to act. Fiscal credibility helps determine the room available to exercise it. France's challenge is to restore that room without sacrificing the social consent on which effective government depends.
Marine Le Pen may change the political conversation. She cannot repeal the arithmetic.

Title: Lindung 24 Jam offers income support, rehab after accidents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An accident can turn a worker's life upside down, with recovery often requiring more than medical treatment. Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed said its Lindung 24 Jam scheme provides eligible workers with access to treatment and rehabilitation following accidents occurring outside working hours.
Under its "Care Beyond Compensation" approach, eligible workers can receive rehabilitation equipment and injury-related implants, as well as physical rehabilitation at Perkeso's rehabilitation centres.
"This includes treatment at government hospitals or Perkeso panel hospitals, funding for rehabilitation equipment and injury-related implants, as well as physical rehabilitation at Perkeso-managed centres and access to vocational support to help workers return to their normal lives and jobs.
"This approach is important because the impact of an accident goes beyond medical bills, affecting income and the financial well-being of the worker's family," he told the New Straits Times.
Introduced on June 1, Lindung 24 Jam complements other Perkeso protections, with benefits subject to eligibility requirements and the nature of the injury.
Azman said a major challenge for workers involved in accidents was the possibility of disability that could affect their ability to work and disrupt their income.
"Typically, employers provide full wages for the first two months of medical leave, followed by half wages if the leave is extended into the third and fourth months.
"However, workers may no longer receive wages if they have to remain on medical leave from the fifth month onwards.
"Lindung 24 Jam helps ease this burden through the Temporary Disablement Benefit, which replaces income during approved medical leave.
"This helps ensure that workers' income is not disrupted when they suffer accidents outside working hours."
Under Section 52 of the Employees' Social Security Act, employers are also prohibited from dismissing or penalising workers while they receive Perkeso's Temporary Disablement Benefit.
If an injury results in permanent disability or death, other benefits are available, subject to the stipulated conditions.
These include Permanent Disablement Benefit, Dependants' Benefit and Funeral Benefit.
For workers who rely on daily wages, even a brief illness or injury can affect their ability to meet daily expenses and support their families.
Income replacement through the Temporary Disablement Benefit under the Employment Injury Scheme is therefore an important component of social protection.
Azman said personal insurance and Perkeso protection served different but complementary purposes.
While private medical insurance generally covers treatment according to the terms of the policy, Perkeso provides a broader social security safety net that can include income replacement, rehabilitation and long-term benefits, depending on the circumstances.
"Perkeso protection is not merely about cash payments when misfortune strikes. It covers treatment, rehabilitation, income replacement and long-term benefits, depending on the type of injury or circumstances.
"Having personal insurance does not necessarily mean a person no longer needs social security protection.
"The most important message is that accidents can happen at any time, anywhere and under any circumstances.
"Lindung 24 Jam was introduced to provide workers and their families with an additional layer of protection when unexpected risks arise," Azman said.

Title: PN logo use, Negri crisis among key court cases this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional  will know this week whether it can use its logo in the upcoming Melaka polls, with the High Court here set to hear its application to stay the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) suspension order on Thursday.
The application is among four high-profile court cases scheduled for this week, including two related to the Negri Sembilan  crisis and a defamation-related contempt action.
The  High Court here had earlier allowed PN to proceed with a judicial review of two RoS notices but refused to suspend the order pending the outcome of the review.
PN is seeking to quash a suspension order dated Sept 23, issued under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. The order suspended all PN activities except those related to responding to a notice of intention to cancel its registration.
The other notice, dated Sept 22, proposed cancelling PN's registration and gave its chairman 30 days to make representations.
The outcome could have significant implications for the coalition, with the Melaka election scheduled for Nov 14.
Meanwhile, the Court of Appeal in Putrajaya will hold case management today  for an appeal by Datuk Mubarak Dohak and five others against a July 8 High Court decision allowing Negri Sembilan's Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, to initiate contempt  proceedings against them over an alleged breach of a June 5 injunction.
The High Court had also refused to stay the contempt proceedings pending their appeal, prompting them to seek a stay from the Court of Appeal.
On July 29, the appellate court granted an interim stay barring the Seremban High Court from proceeding with the contempt case. On Sept 7, it reserved its decision on the stay application.
The six include Mubarak, the disputed Undang Luak Sungai Ujong; Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, the disputed Undang Luak Jelebu; and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, the disputed Undang Luak Rembau.
The others are Johol Undang Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri and Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, whom the DKU says was removed as Shahbandar Sungai Ujong on July 30.
Separately, the Seremban High Court has fixed Wednesday for case management of a suit filed by 10 former Negri Sembilan  executive councillors challenging the validity  of their removal.
The revocation was gazetted by order of  Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, citing a breach of their pledge of allegiance.
The High Court will also hear a committal application today  by  entrepreneur Christy Ng and her company against J. Vikneshvra Rau, who operates the "archnionverse" Threads account.
The application stems from Vikneshvra's alleged failure to comply with a court order  to publish a full-page  apology in two major newspapers after a defamation suit over statements he posted last year.

Title: 38,000 rejected claims expose gap in workers' safety net
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Over the past decade, more than 38,000 workers injured in accidents suffered a second blow when the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) rejected their claims, classifying the incidents as non-employment related.
Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the figure, recorded between 2015 and 2025, exposed a significant gap in social protection for workers injured outside working hours, particularly those without private insurance or takaful coverage.
The gap persisted in more recent years, with 12,306 claims rejected by Perkeso between 2023 and October last year because the injuries were classified as non-employment-related.
He said the figures highlighted the need for a broader safety net that protected workers beyond the workplace.
"Such a high number of cases required immediate intervention to ensure workers in Malaysia remained protected, not only during working hours but also outside working hours," he told the New Straits Times.
Khairul Firdaus said the issue was particularly pressing for B40 and some M40 workers, many of whom could not afford the monthly premiums for private insurance or takaful after prioritising basic household expenses.
Citing Bank Negara Malaysia data, he said personal insurance or takaful ownership among B40 workers remained low, at between four and 30 per cent, compared with 88 per cent among higher-income urban workers.
He said the introduction of the Lindung 24 Jam scheme on June 1 aimed to close the gap by extending social protection to non-employment accidents.
Under the scheme, workers contribute 0.75 per cent of their monthly wages. A worker earning RM1,500, for example, contributes about RM11.25 a month.
Khairul Firdaus said the low contribution could provide crucial support to workers who suffered serious injuries or disabilities from accidents outside working hours.
"When B40 or M40 workers suffer serious injuries or disabilities due to accidents outside working hours, they can lose their source of income and become exposed to financial risks that can severely affect their lives.
"Lindung 24 Jam helps close this gap by providing protection around the clock, including income replacement and benefits for dependents."
The scheme has already recorded a sharp increase in claims since its introduction.
Between June 1 and July 31, a total of 2,751 claims were submitted, averaging 45 a day.
Perkeso approved RM3.45 million in benefits for 2,508 recipients in July alone, bringing the total benefits paid during the first two months to RM4.69 million.
More than 90 per cent of claims were approved and processed within five days, Khairul Firdaus said.
The largest share of benefits went towards rehabilitation equipment and implants, amounting to RM3.69 million cumulatively, followed by more than RM909,800 in Temporary Disablement Benefits to replace income during medical leave.
Additionally, long-term benefits for dependants exceeded RM2 million.
Khairul Firdaus said more than half of Lindung 24 Jam beneficiaries after the first two months were lower-income workers earning below RM3,500 on average, while the remainder were from the M40 group.
He said most beneficiaries were workers involved in everyday accidents outside working hours.
The figures, he said, showed that accidents outside working hours were not isolated incidents but a recurring financial risk for workers and their families.
Khairul Firdaus added that Lindung 24 Jam should not be viewed as a substitute for private insurance, but as a complementary layer of protection.
He said private medical cards were generally designed to cover hospital treatment, while Perkeso protection provided income replacement and longer-term support in cases of permanent disability or death.
Among the benefits available under Lindung 24 Jam are Temporary Disablement Benefit, Permanent Disablement Benefit, Dependants' Benefit, Constant Attendance Allowance of RM500 a month, funeral benefits and rehabilitation services through Perkeso facilities.
"Private insurance and Perkeso protection do not overlap. Instead, they complement each other," Khairul Firdaus said.
He added that the scheme was ultimately based on the principle of social solidarity, where contributions help spread financial risks across the workforce.

Title: Melaka polls: Seat deals remain the wild card [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: With less than two weeks before nomination day for the Melaka election, the battle lines are taking shape as Barisan Nasional, Pas and Pakatan Harapan signal their readiness to contest.
But despite preparations being well underway, uncertainty over political cooperation and seat negotiations means the final electoral landscape may not be clear until nomination day.
BN and Pas have indicated that their candidate lists are ready, while PH has finalised seat allocations among its components, PKR, DAP and Amanah.
The question now is whether the parties will stick to their respective plans or strike last-minute deals to avoid multi-cornered contests.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said early candidate preparations demonstrated organisational readiness and allowed parties to assess candidates' acceptance among voters.
"Announcing candidate lists is not merely about who will contest. It is also closely linked to seat negotiations and political cooperation.
"The real challenge is ensuring that seat allocations are accepted by the parties and their supporters," he told the New Straits Times.
Tawfik said BN held a clear advantage as the incumbent government, backed by its established grassroots network and election machinery.
Having won 21 of Melaka's 28 state seats in 2021, BN is seeking to defend its majority under caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Tawfik believes a proposed BN-plus arrangement involving Pas could further strengthen the coalition's prospects.
"I expect BN-plus, with Pas contesting under the BN symbol, to win at least 24 seats, including three additional seats in Bemban, Sungai Udang and Bukit Katil."
However, Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia political scientist Dr Syaza Shukri said the political landscape remained fragmented, with parties seemingly preparing to contest independently.
"There are still many unanswered questions. We may have to wait until nomination day to see how political cooperation takes shape."
Syaza said BN and Perikatan Nasional currently appeared to have an advantage over PH, but questioned whether BN could increase its seat tally.
"I don't think BN can win more seats. In 2021, it won several constituencies by narrow margins. BN's strength in Melaka is not as dominant as in Johor."
She added that even cooperation between BN and PN might not increase BN's tally if some constituencies had to be allocated to its partners.
For Rauf, the election will also test whether his administration's grassroots engagement can translate into electoral support.
His "Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat" programme, aimed at engaging the public, has covered all 28 constituencies, attracting more than 100,000 participants and recording 5,170 complaints for follow-up action.
Rauf has cited an 80 per cent approval rate for the initiative.
Meanwhile, PH faces the challenge of defending its five seats, while Bersatu's prospects could be affected if Pas reaches an agreement with BN.
Tawfik cautioned that poorly coordinated seat arrangements could lead to multi-cornered contests and split votes.
He said candidate acceptance, grassroots machinery, local issues and voter turnout would be key to the election outcome.
For now, the parties may have their candidates ready, but Melaka's battle lines remain unsettled.
Whether BN can defend or expand its majority will depend on the alliances forged, candidates fielded and their ability to turn grassroots support into votes.

Title: 'Our job is to be right, not popular,' says Chief Justice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The judiciary must earn public confidence through integrity, transparency and accountability rather than chase popularity.
Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh said that social media had intensified scrutiny of court decisions, with judgments often condemned or praised before the public had read the legal reasoning behind them.
"Our job as judges is not to be popular. Our job is to be right," he said.
He was delivering a lecture titled "Justice on Trial: Can the Judiciary Survive the Court of Public Opinion?" to law students at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) in Kuala Terengganu yesterday.
Wan Ahmad Farid said the distinction between public confidence, which the judiciary must earn, and public approval, which it must not pursue, was central to preserving judicial independence.
Courts were not designed to be popular, he said, as judges were sometimes required to protect unpopular defendants, uphold rights and rule against powerful interests.
"A judiciary that is always popular is probably not doing its job," he said.
He identified three major challenges facing the judiciary: public suspicion arising from past controversies, the speed and distortion of information on social media, and the tendency to judge courts by their rulings rather than the processes behind them.
Wan Ahmad Farid said the judiciary had endured difficult periods, including the 1988 crisis, when the then Lord President Tun Salleh Abas and several Supreme Court judges were suspended, with some later removed from office.
The 2007 Lingam video controversy further damaged public confidence after a secretly recorded video showed prominent lawyer Datuk V.K. Lingam discussing judicial appointments over the telephone.
The recording raised concerns about alleged attempts to influence the appointment and promotion of judges, prompting a Royal Commission of Inquiry.
The commission found the clip authentic and concluded that the actions of several individuals had seriously undermined the independence and integrity of the judiciary.
Wan Ahmad Farid said the judiciary must acknowledge such failures and pursue rigorous self-correction rather than conceal its weaknesses.
He also warned that social media had widened the gap between what courts decided and what the public believed they had decided.
A lengthy judgment could be reduced to a screenshot within minutes, he said, with online commentators quick to label judges heroes or villains without reading the full decision.
He urged the public to read judgments, including dissenting opinions where available, before forming an opinion.
Citing a recent High Court decision acquitting a teenager of murder on grounds of insanity, he declined to comment on the merits as the case was on appeal. However, he said the public reaction illustrated how grief and anger could shape perceptions before the court's reasoning became available.
"When a court is judged by the outcomes it produces rather than the process it follows, it has already lost the argument about its legitimacy," he said.
Wan Ahmad Farid warned that sustained online pressure could compromise judicial independence, even without direct interference, if judges became hesitant to make unpopular decisions for fear of public backlash.
He also cautioned against trial by media and social media, while adding that contempt powers must not be used to silence legitimate criticism.
They should be used with restraint and clear justification to protect fair trials, while recognising freedom of speech.
To strengthen public trust, he outlined four principles: explaining decisions in accessible language, protecting due process, defending judicial independence without personalising disputes, and ensuring genuine accountability.
Courts should publish plain-language summaries, timely judgments and clear explanations of decisions.
Judicial independence, he added, must not be mistaken for immunity from scrutiny. He said that credible ethical standards and fair, transparent complaints procedures were essential to accountability.
He also called on government and political leaders to ensure that disagreement with judicial decisions did not turn judges into enemies, while urging the Attorney-General's Chambers and the Malaysian Bar to uphold the rule of law publicly.
Wan Ahmad Farid called on future lawyers to read judgments before commenting, criticise legal reasoning rather than personalities, defend the institution even when they lost a case, and explain the law to the public without condescension.
He said criticism of judicial decisions was healthy, but attacks that undermined the institution risked weakening respect for court orders and the rule of law.
"The threat today is no longer a leaked video shouting 'correct, correct, correct'. The threat today is the democratisation and normalisation of outrage," he said.
Despite the challenges, he expressed confidence that the judiciary could withstand the court of public opinion, provided it remained committed to legality, independence and integrity.

Title: Lindung 24 Jam: Protection that goes beyond the workplace
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mohd Ridhuan Zaini, 46, was left reeling after paying RM4,800 out of his own pocket for surgery following a motorcycle accident that left him with a fractured shoulder.
The driver, who has more than 20 years of experience, declined to work on a Saturday in December last year due of a family commitment. Later that day, he skidded and fell while riding his motorcycle, leaving him injured and unable to work for more than a month.
Without personal medical insurance, Ridhuan had to rely on his company's medical coverage, as he was not eligible for Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) protection because the accident occurred outside working hours.
"I thought the Lindung 24 Jam scheme had already taken effect by then, but it had not.
"When I checked with my company, I was told that the coverage was only for accidents during working hours, so I had to rely on my company's medical coverage to get treatment," he told the New Straits Times.
Ridhuan initially sought treatment at a university hospital but was told he would have to wait a week for surgery. Unable to endure the pain, he later opted to go to a private hospital.
Although his company provided medical coverage, it wasn't enough for the treatment.
His recovery was further complicated by the loss of overtime while he was on medical leave, leaving him with only his basic salary. He also struggled to afford follow-up treatment, with each appointment costing more than RM200.
"Because of the cost, I only went for one follow-up. At the time, I was only receiving my basic salary, which was significantly lower without overtime payments.
"When I saw the medical bill and realised I had to pay RM4,800, I wanted to run away," he said.
OFF-HOUR PROTECTION
Ridhuan said the introduction of Perkeso's Non-Employment Injury Scheme, also known as Lindung 24 Jam, would provide workers with protection against accidents outside working hours.
"I wish it had been introduced sooner. It would have provided a social safety net for people who have jobs like me."
Introduced on June 1, the scheme extends social protection to eligible workers who suffer non-work-related accidents, regardless of when or where they occur.
[[nid:1558588]]
Perkeso group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed said 8.5 million workers, or 87.6 per cent of those eligible, remained enrolled in the scheme, reflecting the importance workers placed on protection beyond working hours.
He said workers spent 33 per cent of their time each year working, including commuting to and from work, leaving the remaining 67 per cent, or about 244 days, outside the scope of conventional employment-related protection.
He added that the scheme received 6,330 claims in its first three months, from June 1 to Aug 31, averaging 69 claims a day.
A total of RM9.97 million in benefits was paid during the period, covering temporary and permanent disablement, medical expenses, funeral benefits, dependants' benefits, rehabilitation equipment and implants.
However, Azman said 52 per cent of workers earning below RM3,500 had opted out of the scheme.
He expressed concern that many workers in this income group did not have private insurance, leaving them vulnerable to financial hardship.
'IT WAS A GREAT HELP TO US'
For 32-year-old housewife Syahirah, the scheme provided financial support when her husband suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury while playing football on a Sunday.
She said her husband received RM540 under the scheme and that the claims process was straightforward, requiring only a copy of the claimant's identity card, a bank account statement and the original medical certificate (MC).
"As my husband's medical leave (MC) was issued in stages, Perkeso processed each claim separately after the respective MC period ended.
"We submitted the first claim on July 7, and the payment was credited into his bank account on July 13. The process was very fast."
The payment helped ease the family's financial burden during her husband's recovery.
Although he had a private medical card, it did not cover income lost while he was on medical leave.
"Alhamdulillah, Lindung 24 Jam has been a great help to us. I advised my husband not to opt out of it because it provides protection that our medical insurance does not," Syahirah said.
Another claimant, who identified herself only as Mimi, received RM180 as temporary disablement benefit after injuring her left leg when she fell into an uncovered drain while picking up her child after work on June 26.
She submitted her claim on July 6 and received the payment on July 22.
"The claims process was simple. I submitted my application through the Lindung24 portal by filling in the required information and uploading the necessary documents," said Mimi.
"Perkeso then contacted my employer for verification before the payment was credited."
The experience made her realise the importance of protection against accidents outside working hours.
"Only after experiencing the accident myself did I realise how important it is to have protection for accidents that happen outside working hours," she said.
Another claimant, who requested anonymity, received RM304 after being placed on 17 days of medical leave following an accident.
She submitted her claim on July 6 and received the payment on July 24.
While describing the application process as straightforward, she called for greater transparency in how compensation was calculated.
"It would be helpful if claimants could receive an email or a statement explaining how the compensation amount is calculated," she said.
'IT GIVES ME PEACE OF MIND'
For younger workers who cannot afford private medical insurance, Lindung 24 Jam offers an additional layer of protection against unexpected accidents.
Private company protege Syaf, 26, said the lack of a medical card made the scheme an important safety net, particularly as she commuted about 6km between her rented home and office.
"One unexpected accident could quickly become a financial burden.
"The medical benefit was the main factor. At the moment, I cannot afford a medical card, so this scheme gives me some peace of mind knowing I have protection if I am involved in an accident outside working hours.
"At least I can receive treatment or make a claim for eligible medical expenses."
Syaf said the monthly contribution was more affordable than private medical insurance plans she had considered, many of which cost more than RM80 a month.
For 25-year-old company secretary executive Danish, the decision to remain covered was largely driven by his daily commute.
He travels about 70km by motorcycle to work each day and said financial commitments had prevented him from taking out private medical insurance.
"My main consideration was my daily commute. Since I ride a motorcycle almost every day, the risk of an accident is always there.
"I do not have a medical card because of financial constraints. My current commitments do not allow me to get one, so I think it is better to be protected under Lindung 24 Jam.
"Perkeso is an affordable option for people like me because the monthly deduction is much lower, with the maximum contribution capped at RM45 a month."
The scheme is being implemented in three contribution phases, starting at 0.75 per cent of monthly wages and fully borne by employees, subject to a wage ceiling of RM6,000.
