Title: Ex-Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman faces 'high legal hurdle' in bid to block MACC asset notice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Yayasan Bank Rakyat (YBR) chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin's bid to block an asset declaration notice from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) faces a high legal hurdle.
Senior lawyers have questioned the prospects of his injunction application, filed amid an investigation into suspected misappropriation and abuse of position involving a RM10 million YBR investment.
Bar Council Criminal Law Committee chairman Vivekananda Sukumaran said courts generally decline to interfere with MACC's investigative powers, while legislation imposed further restrictions on injunctions against public authorities.
"The court can hear such an application, but the bar is very high, and our courts have consistently declined to interfere with MACC's investigative steps," he told the New Straits Times.
Nazir and his elder brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain, filed an originating summons at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Tuesday, seeking a declaration that Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009 is unconstitutional.
They also want an injunction preventing MACC from issuing or serving asset declaration notices against them. Case management is scheduled for today.
Courts reluctant to interfere
Vivekananda said Section 36 empowers senior MACC officers, acting on reasonable grounds arising from investigations, to demand declarations covering property, income and how assets were acquired.
He cited a Federal Court ruling involving lawyer Latheefa Koya, which established limits on judicial review of criminal investigations.
The Court of Appeal applied the same principle in May 2024 when it dismissed a challenge by the late former finance minister Tun Daim Zainuddin and his family against MACC's investigation and related notices.
Vivekananda said the Specific Relief Act 1950 also restricted injunctions interfering with government departments carrying out their public duties.
"Going to court is a legitimate right, but filing an application does not suspend the law. A pending application is not a court order," he said.
However, he said that MACC's actions could still be challenged where there was evidence of bad faith.
"MACC answers to the courts, but bad faith must be proved with evidence, and the door is narrow," he said.
Nazir has alleged the proposed asset declaration notice was issued in bad faith and infringed constitutional protections against self-incrimination.
Criminal lawyer Datuk Dr N. Sivananthan also questioned the attempt to restrain MACC from exercising its statutory powers.
Sivananthan said asset declarations allowed investigators to determine whether an individual's wealth was consistent with their known income.
[[nid:1558552]]
"They don't go and ask every Tom, Dick and Harry to declare. This person is already under investigation. As part of that investigation, they ask him to declare his assets.
"But you are now asking the court to prevent them from asking you to declare. I really don't see how that is going to work," he said.
Sivananthan said individuals who needed time to retrieve financial records could seek extensions from MACC.
RM10 million investment under scrutiny
The dispute stems from MACC's investigation into a RM10 million investment made by YBR during Nazir's chairmanship.
YBR, an educational foundation established by Bank Rakyat, receives funding from the cooperative bank and contributions linked to its members' dividends to support educational initiatives.
Its audited 2022 annual report shows the foundation signed an agreement on Nov 16, 2020, to subscribe for RM10 million in redeemable preference shares in Precious Amber International Berhad (PAIB).
The report records redemption of the investment on Dec 10 and 15, 2022.
PAIB subsequently faced regulatory action from the Securities Commission (SC), which issued a cease-and-desist directive on March 4 last year, after finding the company had held itself out as conducting fund management activities without the required licence.
In December, the SC described statements made by PAIB to investors as inaccurate and misleading and confirmed the company had been placed on its Investor Alert List.
The regulatory action came years after YBR's investment and does not establish wrongdoing in the original transaction.
Nazir has denied wrongdoing, maintaining that YBR recovered its RM10 million investment and earned RM1.85 million in returns.
He also disputed allegations that Mubarak owned PAIB when YBR invested, saying his brother acquired an interest several months later.
During the investigation, MACC reportedly seized 15 luxury cars worth about RM31 million, 12 high-powered motorcycles valued at RM5 million and other assets.
The NST has reached out to the MACC for further updates on the case.
Refusal does not automatically mean offence
MACC said
Nazir refused to accept
an asset declaration notice on Oct 14, citing his pending court application.
[[nid:1558551]]
However, Malaysia Corruption Watch (MCW) president Jais Abdul Karim said refusing to accept a notice, challenging its legality and wilfully failing to comply were separate matters.
"These three circumstances cannot be arbitrarily treated as the same," he said.
Jais said the validity and proper service of a notice must be established before conclusions about non-compliance could be drawn.
Under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act, wilful failure to comply with a valid notice carries imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to RM100,000 upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'France is burning': Trump blames immigration for unrest, urges border crackdown
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules.
"France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. "Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!"
France was reeling Sunday from widespread damage during protests the day before that left a historic town hall torched and led to 1,800 arrests, piling pressure on President Emmanuel Macron six months before elections to replace him.
Trump's post comes after similar comments made by Vice President JD Vance on Saturday.
"Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn't listen," Vance wrote on X.
"I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn," he added.
Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on Nov 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well.--AFP

Title: Malaysian honoured for boosting Japan ties
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian educator and cultural exchange advocate Gary Tang has received the Japanese Foreign Minister's Commendation for helping to strengthen Malaysia-Japan relations.
Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki said Tang was one of two Malaysians selected this year among 159 individuals and 67 groups honoured worldwide.
"With his remarkable vision and leadership, Tang has made significant contributions in advancing Japan-Malaysia cooperation across education, culture, business and many other fields," said Shikata at the presentation ceremony at his official residence on Saturday.
He said Tang had played a pivotal role in promoting study opportunities in Japan among Malaysian youth since becoming president of the Japan Graduates' Association of Malaysia (Jagam) in 2018.
Tang, as a governor of the Asean Council of Japan Alumni, also led the launch of its Business Advisory Board last month to strengthen connections between Japanese companies and the Asean market.
In cultural exchange, Jagam has co-organised the Pavilion x Jagam Matsuri at Pavilion Bukit Jalil since last year, featuring traditional Japanese performances and cultural activities.
In his acceptance speech, Tang said the commendation reflected the support and cooperation of his family, mentors, colleagues and partner institutions.
Tang travelled to Japan in March 1983 before enrolling at Kokusai Gakuyukai, now associated with the Japan Student Services Organisation.
He later joined the Malaysia Students Association in Japan, serving as its president in 1986.
Tang said two Japanese values — sonkei (respect) and kansha (gratitude) —  were his lodestars in education, culture and personal relationships. — BERNAMA

Title: France protests descend into looting as 1,500 businesses suffer damage
Article:
PARIS: French police battled protesters and looters for a second day Sunday as the country reeled from the violent chaos left by a day of cost-of-living demonstrations in which 2,000 people were arrested nationwide.
Paris city workers had not finished clearing up the torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris from Saturday's unrest when the new troubles started and political recriminations erupted.
AFP journalists said several hundred people gathered in the Republique square in the capital following social media calls for a gathering that authorities said had not been approved.
Television footage showed the looting of a clothing store and bikes were also set alight nearby.
[[nid:1558535]]
The Paris police prefecture said security forces moved in when "faced with the initial signs of tension."
AFP journalists saw police firing tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered in the square. Bottles and rocks were hurled at police who made several arrests.
SOME 500 IN CUSTODY
Some 550 people out of 855 arrested in Paris remained in detention from Saturday's troubles and police stations were struggling to cope, according to the Legal Team Paris group of lawyers.
- GOVERNMENT UNDER PRESSURE -
Six months from a presidential election, the government faced opposition attacks over preparations for the nationwide day of action that followed weeks of mounting student protests over conditions in schools.
President Emmanuel Macron, who Saturday vowed that anyone who engaged in vandalism or looting would be prosecuted, was to address the nation Sunday evening at 1800 GMT.
Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate for the National Rally party, said the troubles showed that Macron's administration was "running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented."
"We are experiencing a profound crisis of trust and authority, which poses a threat to democracy," said Le Pen, who leads opinion polls ahead of the election.
Le Pen has blamed ultra-left groups, while Jean-Luc Melenchon head of the far-left France Unbowed party accused authorities of inflaming tensions.
[[nid:1558534]]
With images of French town halls burning and shops being looted grabbing headlines around the world, US President Donald Trump waded into the debate, blaming immigration for the unrest.
"France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country," Trump said in a social media post.
Looting rampages were reported Saturday in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, on the margins of protests over the cost of living.
Around 1,500 businesses were damaged with losses estimated at hundreds of millions of dollars, according to the Retail and Trade Federation. One person died during the main march in Paris, but officials said the case was health-related.
"It's like we had a war," a 78-year-old Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told AFP amid burnt street barricades from the protests.
- 'ANIMALS' -
Another resident, Anita Gras, said she saw young men loot a sports shoe retailer.
"It's appalling, terrifying – groups of young people came here yesterday, looting, smashing everything, with total impunity," said 57-year-old Cecile Rogue surveying a pile of charred bicycles.
The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire that local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI had been deliberately set by "a wild horde."
About 7,000 people staged a march in the central city on Sunday to show their anger at the devastation.
In Lyon, a store owner, Jean-Christian, said those behind the violence were "animals."
"We saw them looting, men high on adrenaline."
A tourist office in the city centre was set ablaze during the protests amid multiple clashes and looting.
On Sunday, a clothing store was also looted in Lyon.
- TOURISTS STUNNED -
In Paris, startled tourists were seen Saturday running with suitcases along streets filled with tear gas and protesters.
A Danish tourist, Soren Petersen, said it was "sad" to see damage to Paris buildings. "It is not a protest, it's far beyond a normal protest," he told AFP.
Around 500 police, firefighters and paramedics were hurt in the protests, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.
The violence took place on the sidelines of nationwide protests that the interior ministry said drew 550,000 people. The CGT union said 800,000 people participated.
A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Etienne. In Mulhouse a 17-year-old girl lost an eye, according to prosecutors.
France's Yellow Vest movement, which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron's government over planned fuel-tax hikes, had called Saturday's "yellow and youth" demonstrations.--AFP

Title: E-Commerce Bill set for first parliamentary sitting next year
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUANTAN: The E-Commerce Bill, aimed at strengthening accountability among online platforms and sellers, will be tabled at the first parliamentary sitting next year.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the draft was being refined.
"Currently, we do not have specific legislation governing e-commerce. In most cases, we facilitate negotiations by acting as intermediaries between online entrepreneurs or sellers and marketplaces," she said after the closing ceremony of the Retail Access Programme here yesterday.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the 2027 Budget on Oct 9, had announced the government would introduce the bill to regulate e-commerce platforms operating in Malaysia.
In Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia Retail Chain Association president Datuk Liew Bin said the bill was crucial to fostering a healthy digital economy.
"We are not against foreign investment, nor are we opposed to e-commerce growth. Online and brick-and-mortar retail can complement each other," he said.
He added that the proposed legislation would clearly delineate the liabilities of e-commerce platforms and merchants, tighten oversight of non-compliant goods, enhance seller verification and dispute resolution mechanisms, and enforce tax transparency to ensure cross-border sellers compete on an equal footing with Malaysian merchants.
Meanwhile, Fuziah said the Retail Access Programme had assisted 1,862 entrepreneurs from 2023 to this month.
She said the programme served as a stepping stone for micro-entrepreneurs to expand their businesses by showcasing their products and understanding supermarket requirements.

Title: MediAsas plan to offer financial, health safety net to Malaysia's M40: Dzulkefly
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The MediAsas Plan scheme, set to launch in January 2027, will provide a financial and healthcare safety net for Malaysia's middle-income group (M40), who are currently facing medical inflation.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the plan would provide protection to the M40 group through transparent cost control without hidden or excessive charges.
"Currently, a total of 340,000 private insurance policies have been surrendered by policyholders due to not being able to pay private premiums, and (more) people opt to go to government facilities; hence, the ministry comes up with this financial safety net.
"No citizen should fall into poverty just because he or she wants medical treatment; therefore, this MADANI health financial protection comes forward by offering an affordable basic protection scheme," he said in a post on the Facebook platform today.
Dzulkefly said the MediAsas Plan pilot project, held in the Klang Valley since the end of July, also allows policyholders to make flexible payments using the Employees Provident Fund Akaun Sejahtera (Akaun Dua) ​​to ease their monthly burden.
As for vulnerable groups, he said the Tabung Bantuan Perubatan was increased by 50 per cent to RM60 million from RM40 million, specifically to cover high-priced medical devices such as bone implants and heart stents.
He said the government allocated RM80 million to the Peduli Kesihatan scheme for the B40 Group (PeKa B40) programme.
Earlier, the Finance Ministry announced that MediAsas, which provides protection for individuals up to 85 years of age, will be offered as a separate (standalone) medical insurance and takaful protection plan that includes two product options, namely MediAsas Teras (standard plan) and MediAsas Flexi (standard-plus plan).

Title: Macron vows crackdown as France protests leave 2,400 arrested, nearly 1,000 police injured
Article:
PARIS: President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday slammed the "unbridled" violence that erupted in cost-of-living protests across France, as police battled protesters and looters in new clashes in Paris.
Nearly 2,400 people were arrested Saturday in unrest that represented some of the worst urban violence in France in years, with almost 1,000 police and gendarmes injured, seven seriously, the interior ministry said.
In an address to the nation, Macron said local authorities would be able to ban – "if necessary" – certain rallies in coming days. But he stopped short of announcing drastic measures, such as a state of emergency or curfew.
"Tonight, we all feel anger and shame," Macron said of the devastation brought by the protests that include town halls burned down and hundreds of businesses looted or damaged.
"Looking at these images, we all asked ourselves: what is going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" said Macron, who insisted there must be a distinction between protesters with "legitimate demands" and "those who destroyed, smashed, and looted."
[[nid:1558517]]
He vowed the authorities would be "uncompromising" towards the "agitators from ultra-left fringe groups, joined by numerous delinquents" who "unleashed unbridled violence in our cities."
AFP journalists said police Sunday fired tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered in a Paris square following social media calls for a gathering that authorities said had not been approved.
Bottles and rocks were hurled at police who made 42 arrests, according to authorities. At least five stores were looted around Republique square.
Other stores in central Paris also had windows smashed and the city hall told many to close. In the southeastern city of Lyon, police battled youths who attempted to loot a luxury clothing store.
- MACRON CRITICS POUNCE -
The unrest came just months before a presidential election where centrist Macron cannot stand again and Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate for the National Rally party, is riding high in the polls.
Le Pen said the troubles showed that Macron's administration was "running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented."
Jean-Luc Melenchon, head of the hard-left France Unbowed party, also running for president, warned that the country could be heading toward "events that will eventually become uncontrollable."
Macron said "our country deserves a fine presidential election", marked by debates "with the parties, rather than in the streets with violence."
Saturday's protests had seen unions, the anti-Macron Yellow Vests movement that rattled the early years of his presidency and school students, who had protested for the last weeks, join forces in a show of anger at the cost of living and prospects for young people.
[[nid:1558516]]
With images of French town halls burning and shops being looted grabbing headlines around the world, US President Donald Trump waded into the debate, blaming immigration for the unrest.
"France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country," Trump said in a social media post.
- 'ALL NECESSARY LESSONS' -
Macron vowed that top officials would "make decisions in coordination with mayors to protect our cities, public buildings, and businesses."
He said that businesses that suffered would be supported and vowed there would be "full transparency" over the response by security forces to the protests.
Some opposition politicians have already called for the sacking of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez.
Macron said he had asked Nunez to "draw all necessary lessons", particularly with regard to intelligence gathering and anticipation, adding he expected "clear answers."
"It's like we had a war," a 78-year-old Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told AFP amid burnt street barricades from Saturday's protests.
The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire that local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI had been deliberately set by "a wild horde."
In Lyon, a tourist office in the city centre was set ablaze during the protests amid multiple clashes and looting.
A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Etienne. In Mulhouse a 17-year-old girl lost an eye, according to prosecutors. --AFP

Title: Flood victim count at PPS records slight increase; Royal Malaysian Navy sends 100 personnel to Pangkor
Article:
IPOH, Oct 19 — A total of 156 flood victims from 50 families are seeking shelter at relief centres (PPS) in the Larut, Matang and Selama district as of 8pm yesterday.
In a statement, the Perak State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said 100 victims from 29 families were housed at the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Matang Gelugor, up from 90 victims from 27 families recorded at 4pm.
The centre was opened to accommodate residents affected by flooding in Kampung Matang Pasir and Kampung Matang Gelugor.
Meanwhile, 56 victims from 21 families remain at the PPS at SK Matang following a storm that affected residents in Kampung Changkat Baru Matang, Kampung Teluk Kertam, Kampung Melawati and Kampung Hujung Matang.
Separately, the Western Fleet Command (MPA Barat) has deployed 100 personnel from the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) base in Lumut to assist with humanitarian aid and disaster relief following flash floods in several areas on Pulau Pangkor earlier today.
In a statement, MPA Barat’s Strategic Communications Division said the mission, led by Chief Staff Officer for Operations Commander Abdul Manan Mazlan, involved three Fast Combat Boats (FCB) and two rigid-hull inflatable boats (RHIB) to transport personnel and deliver aid to affected areas.
An RMN helicopter is also on standby to provide aerial support if required.
The RMN has prepared 300 food packs and 425 bottles of mineral water for distribution to personnel involved in cleanup operations, including navy personnel, teachers, private individuals and representatives from various government agencies.
The cleanup efforts are focused on SK Seri Pangkor, as well as a mosque and residents’ homes severely affected by the floods and covered in thick layers of mud.
MPA Barat said it and all units under its command at the RMN Lumut Base remained committed to supporting recovery efforts in the affected areas through close cooperation and coordination with relevant agencies.
The statement said the commitment reflected the RMN’s role beyond safeguarding the nation’s maritime sovereignty, including contributing to public safety and well-being during disasters. — Bernama

Title: Lawmakers to address M40 aid, Madani allocations and Tourism Compliance Focus Zone effectiveness in Dewan Rakyat today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Aid for M40 households, allocations for the Madani school and Kampung Angkat programmes, and the effectiveness of the Tourism Compliance Focus Zone (ZTPP) programme are among the issues scheduled to be raised at the Dewan Rakyat sitting today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament website, Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah) will ask the Finance Minister to explain measures to help M40 households no longer eligible for targeted aid but affected by rising living costs, including a mechanism to reassess eligibility based on current income and expenditure.
Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman anak Begri (GPS-Betong) will ask the Finance Minister to explain the detailed breakdown of the RM50 million and RM200 million spent on the Madani School and Kampung Angkat programmes, to ensure transparency over the financial impact and the actual number of beneficiaries under the People's Housing Programme (PPR).
Another question is from Hassan Saad (PN-Baling), who will ask the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister to state the performance indicators used to assess the effectiveness of the ZTPP programme in reducing complaints of excessive pricing.
Also listed is a question from Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) on the status of implementation of the National Women's Policy 2025-2030 to date.
Meanwhile, Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) asked the Communications Minister whether the ministry plans to extend the social media age limit to online gaming platforms, particularly those with large numbers of child and teenage users.
After the question-and-answer session, the House is scheduled to continue with debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage, following the presentation of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, on Oct 9.
The calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament states that the Budget 2027 debate at the policy stage is from Oct 12 to 22, followed by winding-up sessions by the relevant ministers over four days from Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting runs for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Malaysia prepared to assist Indonesia in tackling forest fires
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Malaysia remains prepared to extend assistance to Indonesia in addressing forest and land fires that have resulted in transboundary haze. Furthermore, Malaysia has proposed a cooperation mechanism at the Asean level to strengthen joint action in tackling this issue.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that he is closely monitoring the situation regarding the fires, which have impacted the health and daily lives of the Malaysian people — leading, for instance, to the closure of schools in several states and areas.
“Malaysia remains ready to provide assistance, just as we have offered previously,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Anwar acknowledged the efforts of the Indonesian government in deploying tens of thousands of personnel and various aerial assets to contain the forest and land fires. He noted that addressing such a disaster is a complex challenge, given the vast scale of the affected areas and unpredictable weather conditions.
He emphasised that this transboundary challenge must be addressed through shared commitment and responsibility, in line with the close ties between the two nations and the spirit of regional cooperation.
“We have proposed a cooperation mechanism at the Asean level to strengthen coordination, preparedness, and collective action in dealing with transboundary haze,” he also said. — Bernama

Title: Hazy Monday dawns, 26 stations across Kuala Lumpur, Johor, Sarawak record poor air
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — Malaysia woke up to another a hazy Monday morning with air quality readings showing 26 monitoring stations across the country recording unhealthy levels at 6am.
