Title: Budget 2027: Don’t miss these tax reliefs when you file your taxes next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Before you file your next income tax return, remember to lookout for existing and new tax reliefs.
Under the recently announced Budget 2027, the list of tax reliefs has been expanded for taxpayers.
If you do not already know, taxpayers can even make claims for artificial intelligence (AI) subscriptions — a first for Malaysia’s individual tax reliefs — alongside existing reliefs for education, healthcare and social security contributions.
The list is quite extensive, so here is what you could claim, what is changing and the limits to keep in mind when filing your taxes.
Existing tax reliefs and what will change
Education and skills training
The existing education fee relief of up to RM7,000 will be expanded to cover qualifying formal education in any field.
Taxpayers can claim fees for their own certificate, diploma, bachelor’s degree, master’s degree or Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) studies at recognised local institutions or professional bodies, subject to the prescribed conditions.
This could cover recognised fields such as business, law, accounting, engineering, information technology, healthcare and the arts.
The proposed changes also cover:
Technical and vocational education and training (TVET)
— Up to RM3,000 for qualifying courses undertaken by the taxpayer or spouse.
Other courses and classes
— Up to RM2,000 for qualifying courses, training and self-enhancement classes unrelated to employment for the taxpayer or spouse.
Children’s tuition
— Up to RM2,000 for qualifying courses, classes or tuition in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), arts, languages and religion.
The RM2,000 limit is shared between the latter two categories, not a separate allowance for each. Both sub-limits fall within the overall RM7,000 relief.
Previously, the RM7,000 education relief was restricted to specified fields, while qualifying up-skilling and self-enhancement courses were covered under separate provisions.
Budget 2027 will look at consolidating these into a broader education and skills training relief.
Lifestyle expenses
The existing lifestyle relief of up to RM2,500 covers reading materials, personal computers, smartphones, tablets and internet subscriptions.
Budget 2027 added:
AI subscriptions
— AI software and app subscriptions for personal use by the taxpayer, spouse or child.
Pet adoption
— Adoption costs for pets from registered animal shelters.
Veterinary services
— Qualifying services for pet vaccinations, spaying and neutering.
All these expenses would fall within the existing RM2,500 limit, rather than qualify for separate allowances.
Medical and health expenses
The existing medical treatment relief will be reclassified as health and well-being relief, with the overall limit remaining at RM10,000.
Existing qualifying expenses include treatment for serious illnesses, fertility treatment, vaccinations, dental care, medical examinations and certain diagnostic tests.
The relief also covers assessment, early intervention and rehabilitation for children aged 18 and below with learning disabilities.
Budget 2027 added:
Postnatal care
— Up to RM3,000 for qualifying services provided by a confinement centre or qualified individual.
Breastfeeding equipment
— Up to RM1,000 for qualifying purchases for children aged two and below, paid for by the taxpayer or spouse.
Expenses are claimable within the overall RM10,000 limit.
Parents’ and grandparents’ care
Taxpayers can currently claim up to RM8,000 for expenses relating to their parents and grandparents, including specified medical treatment, dental care, full medical examinations, vaccinations and care services.
Budget 2027 will be extending the relief to all types of care at home, day-care centres and residential care facilities, rather than limiting it to specified medical-related expenses.
Under the proposal, taxpayers would need a written declaration from the carer, excluding the taxpayer, spouse or children, or a copy of the carer’s work permit.
The proposal also removes the requirement for a registered medical practitioner to verify the parents’ or grandparents’ medical condition.
Sports-related expenses
The existing sports relief of up to RM1,000 covers sports equipment, facility rental or entrance fees, registration fees for eligible competitions, gym memberships and sports training fees.
Budget 2027 has included sports shoes — capped at RM300 — within the overall RM1,000 limit.
The relief covers expenses for the taxpayer, spouse, child or parents, subject to the prescribed conditions.
Domestic tourism
The existing relief of up to RM1,000 for domestic tourism expenses applies to the 2026 year of assessment (YA2026) covers entrance fees to attractions such as museums, zoos, theme parks, national parks, marine parks and geoparks, as well as qualifying cultural and arts programmes.
Budget 2027 proposed extending the relief to YA2027.
Social security contributions
The existing RM350 relief covers qualifying Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributions.
Budget 2027 proposed including mandatory contributions under the Self-Employment Social Security Scheme, or Lindung Kendiri for three sectors which are passenger transport, goods and food transport and hawkers.
The existing relief limit remains at RM350, while a separate additional relief of up to RM150 is proposed for qualifying voluntary contributions to Lindung 24 and Lindung Kendiri across 17 non-mandatory sectors.
The changes are intended to encourage social security coverage among self-employed workers, including gig workers and hawkers.
Other existing tax reliefs taxpayers should know about
Budget 2027 does not replace the full range of existing personal tax reliefs.
Taxpayers may continue claiming other qualifying expenses, subject to the applicable limits and conditions.
These include:
Spouse relief
— Up to RM4,000 for a qualifying spouse.
Disabled individual relief
— Up to RM7,000 for an eligible disabled taxpayer.
Disabled spouse relief
— An additional RM6,000 for a qualifying disabled spouse.
Child relief
— Generally RM2,000 for each qualifying child below 18, with different limits for older children in qualifying full-time education and children with disabilities.
EPF and life insurance
— Relief for qualifying contributions and premiums, subject to the applicable limits.
Private Retirement Scheme (PRS) and deferred annuities
— Up to RM3,000 for qualifying contributions and premiums.
Education savings
— Up to RM8,000 for qualifying net annual savings in the National Education Savings Scheme (SSPN).
For the SSPN, the RM8,000 relief was extended under Budget 2025 for YA2025 to YA2027.
Budget 2027 does not propose another extension.
Other tax measures affecting individuals
Contributions to school public contribution funds
Budget 2027 proposed expanding the tax treatment of contributions to approved School Public Contribution Funds, known as Tabung Sumbangan Wang Awam Sekolah (TSUWAS).
Under the existing provisions, individuals and companies can claim a deduction for qualifying cash contributions, capped at 10 per cent of aggregate income.
Contributions in kind do not qualify.
The proposal would allow approved funds to use contributions for a wider range of purposes, including administrative and operating expenses, repairs and maintenance, equipment purchases and school programmes.
Contributions must meet the applicable approval and administration requirements.
The proposal is scheduled to take effect from YA2027.
First-home stamp duty exemption
Separately from income tax relief, Budget 2027 proposed expanding the stamp duty exemption for Malaysian citizens buying their first residential property.
The existing full exemption for qualifying first homes priced up to RM500,000 applies to sale and purchase agreements executed from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2027, subject to the applicable conditions.
Under the Budget 2027, the exemption would cover qualifying sale and purchase agreements executed from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2030.
The proposed treatment is:
Homes priced up to RM500,000
— Full stamp duty exemption on the instrument of transfer and loan agreement.
Homes priced above RM500,000 and up to RM750,000
— Full exemption on the first RM500,000 and a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining portion, subject to the applicable stamp duty calculation.
For a qualifying first home priced at RM700,000, the first RM500,000 would be fully exempt, while the remaining RM200,000 would receive a 50 per cent exemption.
The exemption is subject to eligibility requirements, including Malaysian citizenship and first-home ownership conditions.
This is a stamp duty exemption, not an income tax relief claimed through an annual tax return.

Title: EIS benefits rise to RM25,000 as Socso steps up support for jobseekers
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 18 — The Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Employment Insurance System (EIS) helps workers who have lost their jobs rebuild their livelihoods through financial assistance, career guidance and support in securing new employment.
Perkeso deputy chief executive (Operations) Azirruan Arifin said 117,733 jobseekers had secured employment across various sectors between January and August 14 this year through the organisation’s employment support services.
These include career counselling, job searches and matching, registration and placement through MYFutureJobs, open interviews, career fairs and resume preparation guidance.
“These services give contributors faster access to job opportunities that match their experience, skills and labour market needs.
“For contributors who need to upgrade their skills, the EIS also provides training support through active labour market programmes, including reskilling and upskilling to improve their employability,” he told Bernama recently.
Azirruan said one of the main challenges was helping jobseekers secure new employment quickly, particularly when their skills and experience did not meet current industry requirements.
He said Perkeso provided financial and training support to help jobseekers overcome these challenges and improve their chances of securing employment.
For EIS beneficiary Hamdi Ismail, 54, the assistance helped him navigate a career transition after he left his job as a bank clerk to venture into business.
Hamdi began working as a bank clerk in 1993 before leaving the job in November 2018 to pursue entrepreneurship.
He now sells AG Mango Float drinks and grilled sausages in Kampung Laut, Tumpat, with the income helping to cover his family’s daily expenses.
Hamdi said the EIS assistance had supported him during his career transition and helped him plan his next steps.
“Although preparing mango float drinks is relatively simple, selecting the right mangoes is important to ensure quality,” he said, adding that the drinks are sold for between RM2 and RM3.50 per cup, depending on the size.
His previous contributions to Perkeso had also helped him develop his business, and he hoped more Malaysians would contribute to the scheme to secure protection for their future.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan had earlier announced that Perkeso would enhance EIS benefits, enabling contributors to receive total assistance and protection of up to RM25,000 each, effective October 1. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Perkeso is the Malay acronym for Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial, which translates to the Social Security Organisation in English.

Title: Old Socso contributions open door to life-changing stroke rehabilitation
Article:
IPOH, Oct 18 — For five years, a wheelchair was Salinah Osman’s constant companion, confining the once-active massage therapist to a life far removed from the independence she had enjoyed before suffering a second stroke in 2021.
The 58-year-old, originally from Bukit Mertajam, Penang, still remembers the morning she tried to stand up from a seated position, only for both legs to suddenly give way and her right hand to grow weak.
Unlike her first stroke about two decades earlier, the second robbed her of the strength and mobility she needed to practise her profession, which had brought relief and comfort to hundreds of clients through her home-based spa business.
It also kept her away from the community and volunteer work she loved, leaving her dependent on her husband, Md Rasid Mehat, 66, for daily care while she grappled with other health problems, including heart failure and chronic asthma.
“The ordeal was difficult. I could no longer go out to do charity work, and watching my friends continue with it was heartbreaking. From then on, I had to depend on my husband to take care of me,” she told Bernama.
Despite the setbacks, the mother of two refused to give up, seeking traditional treatments and hospital care while praying for a chance to regain her independence.
Her breakthrough came when she learnt about the rehabilitation benefits available to contributors of the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) who had suffered strokes, prompting her to submit an application.
In a turn of events she had hardly imagined, contributions she had made while working in a factory more than 20 years ago became the key to accessing the treatment she needed. Although she had long left factory work to become a self-employed massage therapist, her past contributions continued to entitle her to protection under the scheme.
In April, Salinah was offered an intensive rehabilitation programme at the Sultan Nazrin Shah Perkeso Rehabilitation Centre in Meru here, with the cost fully covered by Perkeso.
She spent nearly four months undergoing treatment and staying at the centre, supported by her case manager, medical officers and other staff, while using advanced rehabilitation equipment to help her regain movement and strength.
Salinah progressed from relying on a wheelchair to walking with a stick, before eventually being able to walk unaided after returning home. — Bernama pic
“The desire to get back on my feet kept me going. At first, I had to train for hours every day despite my asthma, and I wondered whether I could do it.
“But one day, I began to move my hand and feel my leg again. That was when I became confident that I could recover here,” said Salinah, who has also been receiving a Perkeso Invalidity Pension since November 2006, which has risen from RM269 to RM573.69 a month.
In the final months of her rehabilitation, she progressed from relying on a wheelchair to taking steps with a walking stick. She also completed a computer networking course to help improve her business when she is ready to resume work.
Salinah was discharged on September 3, and just a week later, while at home, she was able to discard the walking stick and walk without it.
Having gone from being bedridden and fully dependent on a wheelchair to regaining her mobility, she is now working towards rebuilding her massage business and returning to the community service that once formed a major part of her life.
Perkeso chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed said the centre offered comprehensive stroke rehabilitation combining clinical expertise, various therapies and advanced technology, adding that it was open to everyone who required stroke rehabilitation, not just Perkeso contributors.
“For insured persons who meet the eligibility requirements, Perkeso will fully cover rehabilitation costs, subject to an assessment of their condition and suitability for treatment.
“Those who do not qualify for Perkeso benefits may still receive treatment at the centre on a self-funded basis, subject to the same assessment,” he said in a statement to Bernama.
Dr Mohammed Azman said treatment costs varied according to each patient’s condition, needs and rehabilitation goals. The centre offers physiotherapy, occupational therapy, hydrotherapy, speech and swallowing therapy, neuro-robotic rehabilitation, psychological support and vocational rehabilitation, including its Return to Work (RTW) programme.
Its advanced equipment includes the Cyberdyne Hybrid Assistive Limb (HAL), Luna EMG, Vibramoov, MetaMotus Galileo platform and Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), as well as brain neuromodulation technologies such as rTMS and tDCS, and NESA.
He said Perkeso also focused on prevention and long-term protection through its Health Screening Programme, introduced in 2013 to help detect non-communicable disease risks early.
Contributors whose ability to work was impaired by stroke could be considered for benefits under the Invalidity Scheme, including a lifelong Invalidity Pension, Invalidity Grant, Constant Attendance Allowance and rehabilitation aids, subject to medical certification and eligibility requirements. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Perkeso is the Malay acronym for Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial, which translates to the Social Security Organisation in English.

Title: Flood relief centres shut in Penang, Pahang and Kedah, Perak keeps two open
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Most temporary flood relief centres (PPS) in Penang, Pahang, Kedah and Perak were closed today as floods improved, with only two remaining in operation in Perak as of 4pm.
In PENANG, Seberang Perai Tengah district officer Datuk Kamarul Haizal Koderat said the only centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Seri Penanti in Bukit Mertajam was closed this afternoon, and all 36 victims from 10 families were allowed to return home.
He said the closure followed assessments by the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department and the Malaysian Civil Defence Force, which found the affected area safe for residents to return.
The centre was opened at 8.30pm last night to house evacuees from Kampung Kubang Semang after their homes were flooded due to heavy rain.
In PAHANG, two PPS in Raub housing 26 evacuees from 11 families were also closed at 1pm today.
The Raub District Disaster Management Committee secretariat said all evacuees at Balai Raya Kampung Baru Cheroh and Balai Raya Sempam Baru PPS had been allowed to return home as flood conditions continued to improve.
Meanwhile, in KEDAH, Kubang Pasu District Civil Defence Officer Capt (PA) Mohd Adenin Suhaim said the PPS at Dewan Lembah Keriang in Jitra was closed at 3.30pm today after floods in Mukim Temin receded.
The closure allowed 26 evacuees from eight affected families to return home. The centre had been opened at 11pm last night to house affected residents from Kampung Tradisi and Kampung Baru.
In PERAK, Larut, Matang dan Selama District Disaster Management Committee chairman Mohd Nasrul Menhat said three PPS, at SK Changkat Ibol, Dewan Masjid Al-Wusta Batu 8 and Dewan Perdana Trong, were closed at 1.30pm today.
However, the Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said two PPS remained in operation as of 4pm, at SK Matang Gelugor and SK Matang.
According to the statement, 146 evacuees from 48 families are still sheltering at the SK Matang Gelugor PPS, while 56 from 21 families are housed at the SK Matang PPS following a storm that affected several villages in the area since Oct 14.
The floods hit Kampung Matang Pasir and Kampung Matang Gelugor, while the storm also struck Kampung Changkat Baru Matang, Kampung Teluk Kertam, Kampung Melawati and Kampung Hujung Matang.
Other areas also hit by floods were Kampung Changkat Ibol, Kampung Batu 9 and the Trong and Matang areas.
In a related development, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said in a Facebook post that he had visited flood-hit areas in Pulau Pangkor today, but no PPS had been opened on the island so far. — Bernama

Title: Public Service Dept says Hybrid Workday policy can be used to adapt to haze conditions
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 18 — Department heads in the public service sector can leverage the Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy to adapt to haze conditions in their respective states.
Public Service Department (PSD) director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said that department heads may employ appropriate methods under the HBH framework to ensure that work deliverables or Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for every civil servant are met.
“We have already implemented this hybrid work schedule, and in the context of the current haze, it is essentially a matter of the situation coinciding.
“Therefore, it is up to the department heads to make use of this arrangement. We can certainly utilise the HBH Policy. However, the most important aspect is that KPIs must be established to ensure that output is maintained, even when working in a hybrid manner during these haze conditions,” he said following the ‘Santuni Pesara’ programme held around Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus today.
Also present was the Terengganu Federal Development Department director Datuk Abdul Kahar Abdul Latif.
During the programme, Wan Ahmad Dahlan took the time to visit and present cash contributions as well as basic necessities to three families of retired government servants — Soh Kim Seah, 90; and Rosnani Abdullah, 73; and Mohd Saadum Che Embong, 69.
Meanwhile, he said that the provision of a special financial assistance of RM750 to over one million government retirees, as outlined in Budget 2027, demonstrates the government’s concern for the contributions made by this group.
He noted that the contributions of retirees to national development throughout their years of service are of immense value and should not be forgotten.
“This clearly shows that the government has never neglected retirees who have served the nation. The ‘Santuni Pesara’ programme is also one of the initiatives implemented to honour their contributions,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Masidi: RM18.7b Sabah allocation covers civil service salaries, not just projects
Article:
KUDAT, Oct 18 — The RM18.7 billion allocated to Sabah under Budget 2027 is not solely for development projects, but also covers the operating costs of federal ministries and departments in the state, Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun said.
He said a large portion of the allocation will cover operating expenses, including salaries for about 120,000 federal civil servants working in Sabah.
Masidi said the Education and Health departments are the largest recipients of operating funds, together accounting for more than half of the RM18.7 billion allocation.
“The RM18.7 billion is not entirely for development. We need to understand that the allocation also covers the operating costs of federal ministries and departments operating in Sabah.
“So, it would be inaccurate to assume that the entire RM18.7 billion allocation is intended to address water supply problems and other development needs in the state,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) 2026 Convention here today.
According to him, the budget’s development allocation includes funding for both new projects and the continuation of existing projects currently under way.
He added that Sabah’s development needs continue to grow each year, and existing allocations may not be enough to resolve the state’s long-standing infrastructure problems. — Bernama

Title: Melaka election to see wider use of OCR‑VA system, Election Commission confident after MCMC tests
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Election Commission (EC) have conducted internet connectivity checks at polling centres to test the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system ahead of the Melaka state election, which will take place next month.
State Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications Committee chairman Datuk Fairul Nizam Roslan said one polling centre, Dewan Penyayang at the Lesung Batu Welfare Complex, was found to be unsuitable for the OCR-VA system due to unsatisfactory internet connectivity.
“As such, the polling centre will be relocated to the Machap Baru State Constituency Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) Complex,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the launch of the Barisan Nasional (BN) election machinery for the Alor Gajah parliamentary constituency at Dewan Kampung Permai in Machap Umboo here today. The event was officiated by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Fairul Nizam said MCMC had also submitted a full report to the EC on internet connectivity at the polling centres to facilitate arrangements on election day.
“I am confident that the EC is fully prepared to use the system on polling day, with assistance from the MCMC,” he said.
It was earlier reported that the OCR-VA system would be used more extensively in the upcoming Melaka state election to automatically record and mark voters’ attendance by scanning information on their identification documents.
The system is expected to expedite attendance verification and recording, reduce errors in manual marking, and improve the efficiency of polling staff and the voting process on election day.
A pilot project for the system was introduced during the Negeri Sembilan state election in August this year.
The EC has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10. — Bernama

Title: Singer Yusuf Islam visits grieving Dr Mahathir, offers prayers for late Tun Dr Hasmah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — British singer songwriter Yusuf Islam, better known as Cat Stevens, paid a visit to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today, following the recent passing of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali.
In a Facebook post, Yusuf said he read Al-Fatihah with Dr Mahathir, noting that the couple had been married for 70 years.
“He is 101 years old, by God’s grace,” he wrote.
The gesture drew warm responses from admirers, many thanking the musician for consoling Dr Mahathir in his grief.
“Sitting beside someone during grief is the greatest gift we can give,” one comment read, while others praised Yusuf for bringing strength and comfort to the elder statesman.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on September 28 at the age of 100, closing a revered union that stood among the nation’s most enduring partnerships.
The couple married in Kuala Lumpur on August 4, 1956, after meeting while studying medicine in Singapore.

Title: Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang and Penang schools resume Oct 19, masks encouraged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, and Penang will reopen and resume normal operations tomorrow.
In SELANGOR, the State Education Department (JPN) said that outdoor activities are to be suspended, and students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks.
School administrators are required to continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and pay special attention to high-risk students.
“Parents or guardians who are concerned about their children’s health may choose not to send them to school, provided that they notify the school,” the statement read.
The Selangor Education Department also advised all relevant parties to rely solely on official channels or the schools themselves to obtain accurate and up-to-date information.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN,  the State Education Department has announced that the End-of-Academic-Session Examinations (UASA) scheduled for this period must be postponed and rescheduled by the respective schools, in light of the haze currently affecting the country.
“This directive also applies to all internal examinations conducted by the schools. All outdoor activities must be halted if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100,” the statement read.
In MELAKA, the State Education Department (JPN) said that school administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings provided by the Department of Environment (DOE) and pay special attention to high-risk students.
The Melaka JPN also advised parents, guardians, and the school community to regularly check official communication channels, either the Melaka JPN or the respective schools, to obtain accurate and up-to-date information.
Meanwhile, in PAHANG, the State Education Department (JPN) said that all schools in the Bentong district will continue to operate as usual. However, all outdoor activities are to be postponed until further notice.
All schools in other districts are operating as usual.
“Any changes regarding school operations will be announced through the official channels of the Pahang State Education Department (JPN Pahang) and the respective District Education Offices (PPD),” the statement added.
A similar situation was also reported in Penang, where the Penang Education Department (JPNPP) issued a statement encouraging students to wear face masks and stay well-hydrated, while also requesting that schools ensure an adequate supply of drinking water.
“The JPNPP will continue to monitor air quality developments to ensure that the safety, health, and well-being of students and the educational community remain a top priority,” it stated. — Bernama

Title: Perak shuts all hiking trails in forest reserves from Nov 2 to Jan 17 due to monsoon season
Article:
IPOH, Oct 18 — All hiking trails and recreational activities within permanent forest reserves (HSK) in Perak will be closed to the public from November 2 to January 17 next year due to the monsoon season.
Perak Forestry director Datuk Mohd Basri Abdul Manaf said the directive took into account current risk assessments and the weather outlook report issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
“All hiking trails and recreational activities within Perak’s HSK, including jungle trekking, four-wheel driving and cycling, are prohibited during this period,” he said in a notice posted on the Perak Forestry Department’s official website.
He said the directive had also been circulated to all district forestry offices, ranger offices, police stations, penghulu (village head) offices and relevant agencies for public information and reference.
However, the department’s Hiking Trail Conservation Programme is exempted from the closure. The programme will be held in the HSK areas of Kuala Kangsar, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kinta, Manjung and Perak Selatan from Nov 21 to Dec 26. — Bernama

Title: Nationwide haze surge pushes API past 150 in 26 areas, Pasir Gudang worst at 182
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — A total of 26 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of this afternoon, with Pasir Gudang, Johor, recording the highest reading at 182.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, seven areas in Johor recorded unhealthy readings: Kota Tinggi (179), Larkin (170), Pengerang (168), Batu Pahat (166), Kluang (161), Tangkak (158) and Segamat (156).
In Selangor, five areas also recorded unhealthy readings: Johan Setia (161), Shah Alam (157), Petaling Jaya and Klang (154 each), and Banting (152).
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai recorded the highest reading at 170, followed by Seremban (166) and Port Dickson (152). All three monitoring areas in Melaka also recorded unhealthy readings: Bukit Rambai (166), Melaka City (158) and Alor Gajah (157).
In the Federal Territories, Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 155, while Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded readings of 154 and 152, respectively.
Meanwhile, the areas recording unhealthy API readings in Pahang and Sarawak were Rompin (152), Kuching (155), Serian district police headquarters (IPD Serian) (155) and Samarahan (138).
A total of 41 areas recorded moderate API readings, while one area recorded a good reading.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate air quality, 101 to 200 unhealthy air quality, and 201 to 300 very unhealthy air quality. Readings above 300 are classified as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi confirms Pakatan vetting complete, Melaka candidates to sign bond with RM10m penalty
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has completed vetting candidates who will contest the 16th Melaka state election, including checks with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the selected candidates will also be required to sign a bond set by the party, with fines imposed if they breach its terms.
“If there is a breach, a fine will be imposed. For MPs previously, the fine was RM10 million,” he told reporters after attending the Smart Parents Interactive Hub programme here today.
He said PH will announce its candidates on Oct 24, once the selection process is finalised.
The Communications Minister said PH is expected to select a mix of fresh faces and seasoned politicians, including those with previous election experience, whether as candidates or winners, adding that the line-up also reflects changes to the constituencies PH will contest following discussions with its coalition partners.
“From what I know, although the line-up has not been fully finalised, it will be a combination. Some have experience, some have contested elections before, some have won, and some may have contested in other constituencies,” he said.
The 16th Melaka state election will be held on Nov 14, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
In the previous state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, while PH secured five. — Bernama

Title: Police open two probes into viral issue involving activist and Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 18 — Police have opened two investigation papers following a viral issue involving a social media activist and the Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan, including a robbery case that led to the arrest of two local men.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the cases were being investigated under Sections 341 and 268, and Section 395 of the Penal Code.
He said two local men had been arrested to assist in investigations into a robbery involving a member of the Rohingya refugee community.
“Police take seriously any issue that could potentially undermine public order and community harmony, and will take appropriate action in accordance with the law,” he said when contacted today.
Mohd Yusoff also referred to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail’s statement that 199 criminal cases involving Myanmar refugees had been recorded nationwide from 2022 to August 2026.
On the implementation of the Refugee Registration Document by the Home Affairs Ministry, Mohd Yusoff said it was intended to systematically record refugees’ identities and biometric data, as well as assist the authorities in conducting security vetting and verifying the identities of registered individuals.
He advised the public against speculating or spreading unverified information to allow the authorities to complete their investigations.
Meanwhile, the activist, who was detained yesterday afternoon along with 12 other individuals, was released at about noon today.
The release was greeted by about 50 supporters outside the Kota Bharu District Police Headquarters. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji urges GRS parties to put Sabah first, warns against ego and power struggles
Article:
KUDAT, Oct 18 — All component parties of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) must prioritise the interests of Sabah and the coalition over personal or individual party interests, in order to strengthen the state’s bargaining power at the federal level, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
The Chief Minister of Sabah said the state’s political leverage in negotiations at the federal level must be anchored in the internal cohesion of GRS, rather than being undermined by power struggles for positions or political egos.
“There is no point in praising the unity of others if we are still bickering within the GRS fold itself; for the true strength of Sabah begins with our own unity.
“No (component) party is so large that it no longer needs its partners, and no party is so small that its contributions can be dismissed,” he said while delivering the keynote address at the 2026 GRS Convention at Dewan Tun Mustapha here today.
Also present were GRS deputy chairmen Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, Tan Sri Anifah Aman, Tan Sri Liew Yun Fah, Datuk Ewon Benedick, and Datuk Chin Su Phin, as well as GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
Hajiji also expressed his appreciation to the grassroots members who sacrificed their time, energy, and personal funds to campaign during elections, while reminding leaders not to forget their contributions once they have attained power.
He noted that the decision by certain parties to leave the coalition and go it alone should serve as a lesson one that helps mature the decision-making process and strengthens the foundational principles upon which GRS was established in 2020, all for the sake of the state’s stability.
He emphasised that merely being a local-based party is not enough to win the confidence of voters if the government fails to address the people’s daily challenges or provide economic opportunities.
“The people want a stable government, one that does more than just talk well, it must be capable of solving problems. We might win the battle of speeches on stage, yet still fail to win the hearts of the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MCMC probes Threads content suspected of insulting Negeri Sembilan royal institution
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into content uploaded on the social media platform Threads, suspected of containing insults against the royal institution of Negeri Sembilan.
In a statement today, MCMC said the content in question touches on issues concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
As part of the investigation, MCMC recorded a statement from an individual at the Labu police station.
“Also seized was a mobile phone along with an eSIM for forensic analysis. The case is being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 [Act 588],” the statement read.
MCMC is also examining how the content was disseminated across social media platforms and will work with relevant enforcement agencies should other offences under existing laws warrant action.
MCMC emphasised that freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly, in accordance with the law and with respect for the royal institution.
The commission added that any enforcement action will be carried out based on facts, evidence and due legal process. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: Najib’s house arrest conditions being finalised, but RM50m fine yet to be settled
Article:
JERTIH, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Prisons Department is now in the final phase of drafting regulations and conditions for the implementation of home detention following the conditional pardon decision that allows former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence through this method.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that the matter is being pursued following a letter from the Pardons Board secretariat, which allows the Malaysian Prisons Department to set conditions for the implementation of house arrest.
“The Malaysian Prisons Department is in the final phase, currently drafting it. Our country has never had (house arrest) before, but suddenly there is... In the letter from the Pardons Board secretariat to the Malaysian Prisons Department, it is stated that the Malaysian Prisons Department can impose any conditions.
“So our (the Malaysian Prisons Department) task is to develop a set of regulations that are currently being worked on,” he said to reporters after officiating the launching ceremony of the Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School initiatives of the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) in Felda Tenang, here today.
However, Saifuddin Nasution said Najib is still at Kajang Prison because he has not paid the RM50 million fine, which is one of the conditions for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Last month, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
Recently, Najib’s lead counsel, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said his client would spend the remainder of his prison sentence for the SRC International case with his family at his residence in Langgak Duta, Kuala Lumpur, under a home detention order granted by the King. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi condemns cyberbullying of UM student Ummi after she questioned Najib fine donations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has condemned the bullying and threats directed at Universiti Malaya (UM) student Ummi Umairah Bakhit following views she expressed at a forum.
He also urged all victims of cyberbullying to immediately lodge reports with the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) immediately.
He said that acts of berating or threatening the student, including threats to track her down at the university, did not reflect a proper decorum in communication and should not occur simply because of differences in opinion.
“We can have different views, that’s not a problem. In Ummi’s case, she expressed her views and we know that university students now have the right to speak up.
“So, we should welcome this because she has not violated any laws, nor has she committed any criminal offence. She only addressed matters concerning the crime of corruption,” he told reporters after attending the Smart Parents Interactive Hub Programme here today.
Fahmi said that although some might not agree with the student’s tone or the way she expressed her views, what’s more important was the substance of the points she raised.
He said her views reflected a desire to see Malaysia become a country that supports efforts to combat kleptocracy, while rejecting acts of theft, robbery and corruption.
During the recent open forum with Umno leaders, Ummi Umairah questioned the public’s decision to donate money to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak pay a court-imposed fine of RM50 million.
Her remarks subsequently drew backlash on social media, including comments containing threats against her.
In light of this, Fahmi urged all cyberbullying victims to immediately lodge reports with the police and MCMC to enable the authorities to identify the perpetrators and take action in accordance with the law.
He said MCMC would examine the action that could be taken in connection with the case, emphasising that the commission would act proactively rather than merely wait for reports to be lodged.
Meanwhile, Fahmi expressed his utmost respect for the decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who had reminded the public to observe proper etiquette when communicating on social media.
Fahmi said users should not assume that online posts carried no consequences, including when accounts used were believed to be fake.
He said the MCMC was also investigating several incidents of coordinated inauthentic behaviour (CIB) targeting Sultan Ibrahim and the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
He said over 2,000 pieces of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated or highly offensive content, along with 600 fake accounts, had been identified as insulting His Majesty.
“Preliminary investigations by MCMC found that most of the fake accounts attacking His Majesty on Facebook were believed to originate from overseas, and investigations are ongoing.
“If we positively identify specific individuals, we will strive to bring them to justice,” he added.
Regarding the case targeting Tuanku Muhriz, Fahmi said number of fake accounts were believed to have been created about a month ago before being used to incite discussions containing insults against the royal institutions.
He said some of the accounts had no followers or only one follower, raising suspicions that they had been created for a specific purpose.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the government is studying the need to introduce more stringent regulatory mechanisms, including electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) processes and age verification, to combat cyberbullying on instant messaging platforms such as WhatsApp.
He said although WhatsApp had set a minimum age of 16 for opening an account, the platform continued to pose safety challenges, especially among school students, because communications on the service were protected by end-to-end encryption.
“Under the Online Safety Act 2025 (ONSA), communication services such as WhatsApp are not currently covered.
“As such, I will request that MCMC examine the matter and engage with Meta, which introduced WhatsApp, as the platform itself has set a minimum age requirement,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya and 10 states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 10 states and two Federal Territories until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Baling, Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Padang Terap and Sik, while in Penang, they are Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara.
In Perak, the warning covers Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Larut, Matang and Selama, and Kerian.
In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang.
In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.
In Negeri Sembilan, the warning covers Seremban and Jelebu.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman (Lingga and Pantu), Betong (Kabong and Pusa), and Kuching. In Sabah, they are Kudat (Kota Marudu and Kudat), the West Coast and the Interior.
The warning was issued at 3.10pm and remains in effect until 6pm today. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan finalises Melaka seat allocation but no deal yet with other parties, says PKR sec-gen
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has yet to reach any concrete agreement on possible political cooperation with other parties for the November 14 Melaka state election.
Datuk Fuziah Salleh, who is Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general, said, however, that seat-allocation negotiations among its three component parties — PKR, DAP and Amanah — had been finalised.
She said PH was expected to contest more than 20 state seats, with nine allocated to PKR.
“So far, there has been no concrete agreement on political cooperation with other parties. Seat allocation negotiations among PKR, DAP and Amanah have been completed,” she said.
Fuziah, who is also deputy domestic trade and cost of living minister, was speaking at a press conference after closing the Akses Peruncitan 2026 programme at a hotel here today.
She said PH chairman and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was scheduled to announce the coalition’s list of candidates in Melaka on October 24.
The Election Commission has set October 31 for nomination, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while PH secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two. — Bernama

Title: HRD Corp training grant applications surge after system reforms, says Ramanan
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The surge in Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) training grant applications reflects the positive impact of measures taken to streamline its implementation system, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
He said the reforms have not only facilitated smoother processes but also strengthened organisational governance and transparency, although the transition required time and effort to execute properly.
“In Melaka alone, applications are nearing the 7,000 mark. This shows that more people are seizing the opportunity and demonstrates that meaningful changes are taking place.
“It is not easy to overhaul a system to make it more orderly, transparent, and aligned with good governance. It takes considerable time, and we thank the entire HRD Corp team for their dedication to carrying out these improvements,” he told reporters after attending the HRD Corp ‘Pocket Talk’ Roadshow: From Policy to the People here today.
Also present was HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Shamir Aziz.
Meanwhile, Ramanan said HRD Corp officers will monitor every training class funded through the agency’s existing levy, either on-site or virtually, to ensure courses are genuinely conducted and benefit the target groups.
“I encourage everyone to seize this opportunity, whether they are workers seeking to upskill, graduates looking for employment, or individuals wanting to build new careers,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji recalls mother borrowing RM15 for exam fees as he vows poverty will not define Sabah children
Article:
KUDAT, Oct 18 — Ensuring that poverty does not determine the fate of Sabah’s children or stand in the way of their progress has become a personal mission and commitment for Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said this resolve is rooted in his own life experiences: growing up in poverty, losing his father at a young age, working as a fisherman and a farmer and watching his mother struggle to raise him.
In an emotional account, he recalled how his mother had to borrow RM15 from relatives to pay for his Lower Certificate of Education (LCE) examination fees in 1971, as she wanted to give him a chance to break free from the cycle of poverty through education.
“Parents today face the same challenges in raising their children and providing them with an education. That is why I have firmly resolved to ensure poverty does not determine the fate of our children. Education is what can lift our children out of poverty.
“If the government has the means to remove even one obstacle from a Sabah child’s journey towards progress and success, then at the very least, we must not allow poverty to determine their fate before they even have the chance to try,” he said.
Hajiji, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, said this in his keynote address at the 2026 GRS Convention at Dewan Tun Mustapha here today.
Driven by this commitment, he said he had ensured that the state government increased the allocation for the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) to RM155 million in 2026, up from RM55 million in 2021, to fund the education of students from underprivileged backgrounds.
He said 480,000 students had so far benefitted from 14 educational assistance initiatives under the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development framework, including the BUDI cash assistance, Ihsan Computer Assistance (BAIK) and student flight ticket subsidy (SUBFLY).
Addressing the economic landscape, Hajiji stressed that the Sabah government was now ready to move into a phase of genuine development empowerment to address long-standing issues affecting the people, supported by increased state revenue that had reached RM7 billion annually.
“Efforts to address large-scale infrastructure needs are being set in motion through the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), which includes 173 Public Works Department (JKR) road network development projects and 77 projects related to water treatment plants and supply systems throughout the state,” he added.
He said the Commercial Collaboration Agreement (CCA) with Petronas in 2021 also marked a significant turning point, boosting the participation of local vendors in the oil and gas sector to 499 contracts in 2025, compared with just 133 previously.
“The state government is also committed to continuing Sabah’s pursuit of its rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) at the negotiating table with the Federal Government, guided by facts, financial data and a strong legal basis,” he said.
Hajiji said the state’s ongoing infrastructure and economic development efforts were complemented by targeted welfare initiatives, including the construction of 11,000 homes under the ‘Rumah Mesra SMJ’ initiative to assist vulnerable groups and young couples.
He added that construction would continue, with a target of building 50 ‘Rumah Mesra SMJ’ homes in each state constituency this year to ensure that the benefits of Sabah’s progress were shared by all, including rural and interior communities. — Bernama

Title: Unesco status alone won’t save silat if youth turn away, says Perak MB
Article:
IPOH, Oct 18 — The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Unesco) recognition of
silat
as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity does not guarantee its survival if younger generations increasingly distance themselves from training, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said.
He said veteran
silat
instructors and grandmasters must pass their knowledge to the next generation to keep the martial art alive and ensure it continues to be practised.
“We may have a proud
silat
heritage, but if young people turn away from the training arena, fewer will truly master and appreciate the art,” he said.
State Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah read out Saarani’s speech on his behalf at the opening of the 2026 Gema Warisan Rakan Muda X Himpunan Mahabbah Pendekar today.
Saarani said Malaysia has more than 150 identified
silat
styles, with the martial art declared a National Heritage in 2009 before gaining Unesco recognition as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2019.
“Through regular training, they (youth) can develop discipline, self-confidence, mental resilience and respect for others. These qualities align with the Perak Sejahtera 2030 agenda to develop quality human capital and youth,” he said.
He also cautioned against letting differences in
silat
styles, teaching traditions, and training methods cause divisions, saying they should instead be embraced with mutual respect and a spirit of brotherhood.
“Relations between
silat
schools must continue to be nurtured to ensure the martial art remains a unifying force in society while connecting younger generations with the nation’s history and culture,” he said.
Saarani also expressed hope that the gathering will spur efforts to revive
silat
training centres, mentor young practitioners and strengthen ties between
silat
schools to preserve the martial art for future generations. — Bernama

Title: ‘We cannot sit back’: Malaysia offers aircraft to fight Indonesia forest fires despite dangerously poor visibility
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysia cannot afford to stand by as raging forest fires in Indonesia send thick haze across the region, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today, as the country offered to deploy helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to help contain the blazes.
But Mohamad warned that dangerously poor visibility, reportedly below 50m in affected areas, could hamper aerial firefighting operations and put pilots at risk.
“It is indeed difficult. Even the Japanese team was previously unable to do anything and has since returned to their country. But as a country affected by the situation, we cannot simply sit back and do nothing,” he said, according to
Sinar Harian
.
Speaking to reporters at the 10th National General Assembly of the National Solidarity Association (PerSoNa) in Melaka, Mohamad said the fires were burning deep in remote inland areas, making them difficult to reach by land.
Thick smoke was also preventing aircraft from operating safely.
“Aircraft cannot fly because the haze is extremely thick, with visibility of less than 50m.
“The Air Pollutant Index (API) in Kalimantan has also reached 1,000, indicating an extremely severe situation,” he said.
Mohamad stressed that the safety of pilots and other personnel must remain a priority in any proposed operation.
“We have to be careful. We cannot force pilots to fly in dangerous conditions. We will not do that,” he said.
He said discussions were under way between agencies from both countries to determine what assistance could be provided, taking into account the remote locations of the fires and the severity of the haze.
Senior officials from the Foreign Ministry, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the National Security Council (MKN) were holding talks with their Indonesian counterparts to work out the details of a possible deployment.
“Apart from offering helicopters and water-bombing aircraft capable of carrying water, they are looking at ways Malaysia can help Indonesia extinguish the forest fires that are currently raging out of control,” he said.
Mohamad said the outcome of the discussions would be presented to the Cabinet soon for approval before assistance could be extended to the Indonesian government.
The proposed assistance comes as Indonesia struggles to contain widespread forest and peatland fires that have sent thick smoke across parts of Southeast Asia.
Indonesia has agreed to accept international assistance to tackle the fires, with authorities assessing offers from neighbouring countries.
The transboundary haze has also disrupted daily life in Malaysia, with worsening air quality prompting health concerns and school closures.
In Johor, schools and educational institutions have been ordered to remain closed until October 23 as the state continues to grapple with unhealthy air quality.
The latest crisis has renewed concerns over the recurring impact of forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, which have repeatedly caused severe haze across the region.

Title: Anwar approves RM30m to resurface 600 roads in Perak, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
IPOH, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved a special allocation of RM30 million to resurface 600 roads in residential areas across Perak, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the allocation, through the Sentuhan Kasih Istimewa YAB PMX initiative, uses the savings of the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) from recent years and is now being channelled back to improve public facilities and comfort, according to Bernama.
“In conjunction with the Perak DAP Convention, I announced on behalf of the Prime Minister a special allocation of RM30 million for road resurfacing works in residential areas across the state.
“At least 600 roads can be resurfaced through this allocation. The resurfacing works will begin next month and are expected to be fully completed before Hari Raya next year,” he said.
He said this while speaking at the 24th Perak DAP Annual Convention, officiated by DAP Secretary-General Anthony Loke here today.
The convention was attended by over 1,000 delegates.
Nga, who is also Perak DAP chairman, said the Madani Government’s commitment to safeguarding the people’s well-being is also demonstrated through various initiatives under Budget 2027 that benefit the B40 and M40 groups.
He said among these initiatives are an individual income tax exemption of RM12,000 for certain taxable incomes, as well as Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance of RM200 for 22 million recipients.
Meanwhile, Nga stressed that DAP will not compromise on issues of corruption and misappropriation despite facing various challenges.
He urged all parties to unite in rejecting corrupt practices, which he said could affect the future of the younger generation.
Nga also praised the courage of a Universiti Malaya (UM) student who voiced concerns about corruption in the country.
He, who is also a UM alumnus, said leaders must set a good example for the younger generation through their stance and actions. — Bernama

Title: Kuching, Samarahan and Serian record unhealthy API readings as haze lingers over Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 18 — Kuching, Samarahan and Serian recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm today.
According to the Natural Resource and Environment Board (NREB) website, Serian recorded the highest reading at 155, followed by Kuching 154 and Samarahan 148.
Seventeen districts recorded moderate levels. Among them, Sri Aman recorded the highest at 96, followed by Betong at 93, Lubok Antu at 90, Tebedu at 87, Lawas at 86, Lundu at 85, Kanowit at 82, Sibu at 81.
Sarikei and Samalaju and Belaga each recorded 76, while Bintulu registered 72, Mukah 71, Miri and ILP Miri 53 and Kapit 52.
Bario registered the lowest moderate reading at 51.
Meanwhile, Limbang recorded a good level of 50.
An API reading of 101 to 200 is classified as ‘Unhealthy’, 51 to 100 as ‘Moderate’ and zero to 50 as ‘Good’. — The Borneo Post

Title: E-Commerce Bill to be tabled next year to regulate online transactions, says deputy minister
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 18 — The E-Commerce Bill will be tabled in Parliament at the first meeting next year to strengthen the regulation of online transactions, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh.
She said the initial draft of the Bill has been completed and is currently being refined before it is tabled.
“At present, we do not have specific legislation to regulate e-commerce. So, in most cases, we negotiate and act as intermediaries between online entrepreneurs and platform providers,” she told a press conference after closing the Retail Access Programme 2026 at a hotel here today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 on October 9, said the E-Commerce Bill would be tabled at the next Parliament meeting in an effort to strengthen the accountability of online platforms and sellers.
Fuziah said the Retail Access Programme, which combines training and business matching, has helped 1,862 entrepreneurs from 2023 to October this year.
She said the programme comprised 38 training series and 21 business matching series, involving 103 local brands and 552 stock-keeping units (SKUs).
“This programme allows entrepreneurs to present their products and understand the criteria set by supermarkets, thus identifying opportunities to enter the retail network,” she said. — Bernama
